Debido a los actos realizados por involucrados en el caso, en 2013 se produjeron perdidas de casi EUR 800,000,000 y EUR 3,600,000, lo que llevó a la quiebra a Pescanova.

De acuerdo con elcorreogallego.es; Junio 04, 2020: La Sala de lo Civil del Tribunal Supremo rechazó el recurso presentado por Nueva Pescanova a la sentencia dictada en Diciembre 2016, en la que se desestimaba la petición de que la antigua sociedad afrontara el pago de distintas cantidades, acuerdo que tuvo lugar en 2015 entre las dos empresas. El fallo desestimó la reclamación de EUR 1,090,000 retenidos por Pescanova más los intereses devengados desde 2015 así como otros EUR 800,000 para gastos administrativos.

row.name: Pescanova, Inc
row.position_or_allegation: Ordered to pay a penalty of USD 35,000 for smuggling - June 13, 2013.
row.details: enforcement: Smuggling | US-United States Attorney - Southern District of Florida | United States
row.profile_notes:
According to United States Attorney - Northern District of New York; June 13, 2013: United States Attorney announced that his office has settled a civil action it brought against Pescanova, Inc. (d/b/a Pescanova USA), an international seafood company with offices in Coral Gables, Florida, based upon the company’s exportation, and subsequent re-importation, of 9,600 pounds of Patagonian toothfish (also known as Chilean Sea Bass or Dissostichus eleginoides) on October 24 and December 15, 2010. As part of the settlement, Senior United States District Court Judge Lawrence E. Kahn issued a Consent Decree which authorized civil penalties, forfeiture and permanent injunctive relief against Pescanova. As part of the settlement, Pescanova will pay civil penalties totaling USD 35,000.00, forfeit USD 96,013.76.

According to United States Attorney - Southern District of Florida; February 03, 2011:  United States Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, announced that the Coral Gables-based seafood company Pescanova Inc., d/b/a Pescanova USA (“Pescanova”), was sentenced in federal District Court in Miami on charges related to the attempted import into the United States of approximately 96,984 Kilograms of frozen toothfish (Dissostichus spp.) from Argentina, with a declared imported value of approximately USD 1,200,000, in violation of the Antarctic Marine Living Resources Convention Act ("Antarctic Act"), 16 U.S.C. § 2431, et sec., and the Lacey Act, Title 16, United States Code, Sections 3372(a)(2)(A) and 3373(d)(1)(A). According to the statement in court and case-related records, in December 2009 Pescanova was the importer of record of four cargo containers of Patagonian toothfish, known commonly in the market-place as Chilean Sea Bass, which were landed at Port Everglades, Florida. The fish were shipped by a company in Argentina related to Pescanova through its parent, Argenova, S.A., an international fisheries conglomerate based in Spain. Pescanova intended to market the product in the United States. United States District Court Judge Ursula Ungaro, who accepted a guilty plea in the case in August 2010, also imposed the sentence. The Court specifically took into account the fact that the illegal seafood product had already been forfeited to the United States and sold for USD1,700,000. Based on representations regarding the implementation of an extensive compliance plan, the Court imposed an additional criminal fine of USD 10,000.

According to United States Attorney - Southern District of Florida; August 24, 2010: Wifredo A. Ferrer, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, announced that PESCANOVA INC., d/b/a PESCANOVA USA, ("Pescanova”), a Coral Gables-based seafood company, pled guilty to charges related to the attempted import into the United States of approximately 96,984 kilograms of frozen toothfish (Dissostichus spp.) from Argentina, in violation of the Antarctic Marine Living Resources Convention Act ("Antarctic Act"), 16 U.S.C. § 2431, et sec. and the Lacey Act, Title 16 , United States Code, Sections 3372(a)(2)(A) and 3373(d)(1)(A). According to the allegations in the Information and statements in court, in December 2009 Pescanova was the importer of record of four cargo containers of Patagonian toothfish, known commonly in the market-place as Chilean Sea Bass, which were landed at Port Everglades, Florida. Pescanova’s intention was to market the product in the United States. The declared wholesale value of the toothfish was approximately USD 1,200,000.

row.profile_notes:
According to the leparisien.fr; September 23, 2016: On September 23, 2016, The Court of Appeal of Versailles ordered Jérôme Kerviel to pay EUR 1,000,000 in damages to the Société générale bank for forgery, breach of trust and fraud. Initially, the bank demanded Jerome Kerviel to pay EUR 4,900,000,000 allegedly lost in 2008 due to the fraudulent broker activities of Jerome Kerviel.

According to the lefigaro.fr; September 04, 2014: On September 04, 2014, the Appeal Court of Paris accepted the liberation of Jerome Kerviel if he wears an electronic bracelet.

According to the lepoint.fr; May 19, 2014: On May 19, 2014, Jerome Kerviel was imprisoned in Nice after being arrested at midnight in Menton just as he crossed the French Italian border. At exactly midnight Kerviel was meant to present himself to the authorities so he could begin serving a three-year prison sentence for forgery and embezzlement. Kerviel has spent the last two and a half months walking in Italy. 

According to the bbc.com; March 19, 2014: On March 19, 2014, Jerome Kerviel has lost his appeal against a three-year jail sentence. France's highest court upheld the jail sentence against Jerome Kerviel but ordered a review of the EUR 4,900,000,000 in damages he was told to pay.

According to the lemonde.fr; October 25, 2012: On October 24, 2012, the Court of Appeal of Paris confirmed the first instance sentence imposed on Jérôme Kerviel (five years imprisonment three of which are unconditional, and payment of compensation in the amount of about EUR 4,900,000,000). 

According to the bbc.co.uk; October 05, 2010: On October 05, 2010, Jérôme Kerviel, former Societe Generale trader, was sentenced to five years imprisonment, with two years suspended, by a court of Paris. He was found guilty of forgery, unauthorised computer uses and breach of trust. Kerviel was told to repay the damages in amount of 4,900,000,000 which were lost by the bank through his activity.

According to the reuters.com; January 26, 2008: On January 26, 2008, Jérôme Kerviel was brought into police custody in Paris, suspected of causing a USD 7,000,000,000 loss through rogue trades at Societe Generale, France's second-biggest listed bank.

row.profile_notes:
According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; December 15, 2025: N26 Bank SE must take appropriate and effective measures to establish a proper business organization. This was ordered by the financial regulator BaFin. BaFin has also appointed a special representative who will monitor compliance with the measures and report to BaFin on the progress of implementation. In addition, BaFin has set additional capital requirements and business restrictions for the institution. The bank is no longer allowed to conduct new business with mortgage loans in the Netherlands. The institute is also prohibited from securitizing claims from this transaction.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 21, 2024: The Federal Financial Supervisory Authority BaFin has imposed a fine of EUR 9 200 000 on N26 Bank AG for systematically late submission of suspicious transaction report in 2022. The fine notice is legally binding.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; July 17, 2023: On March 31, 2023, the Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) extended anti-money laundering measures against N26 Bank AG in addition to its order made on May 11, 2021, and specified them. The growth restrictions for new customers and the mandate of the special representative remain in place. Despite some progress, the institution still has deficiencies in its systems for preventing money laundering and terrorist financing. The decision made on March 31, 2023 is final.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; November 09, 2021: On October 05, 2021, the BaFin ordered N26 Bank GmbH to take measures to ensure a proper business organization and to mitigate risks to the institution's operational resilience. In accordance with section 45b (1) sentence 1 of the German Banking Act, BaFin has ordered risk mitigation measures that place limits on customer growth and on certain risk exposures. Customer acquisition is to be substantially reduced with N26 Bank GmbH only permitted to acquire a maximum of 50 000 new customers per month. In addition, the value of exposures secured by mortgages on immovable property may not exceed EUR 500 000 000. This limitation is applicable in all countries in which N26 Bank GmbH operates. A special commissioner appointed by BaFin will monitor implementation of the measures ordered. The order has been final and binding since November 06, 2021. This order should also be considered in relation to the order issued by BaFin on May 11, 2021 to rectify deficiencies related to the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; September 29, 2021: On June 25, 2021, BaFin imposed a fine in the amount of EUR 4 250 000 against N26 Bank GmbH on the basis of section 56 para. 1 no. 69 of the Act on the Detection of Proceeds from Serious Crimes (Money Laundering Act). The decision came into force on July 15, 2021.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 12, 2021: On May 11, 2021, the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) ordered N26 Bank GmbH to implement appropriate internal controls and safeguards and comply with general due diligence requirements, in order to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing. The BaFin also ordered the bank to rectify deficiencies both in IT monitoring and in customer due diligence. In order to monitor the implementation of the measures, the BaFin is appointing a special commissioner. The notice has been final and binding since May 11, 2021.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 22, 2019: On May 20, 2019, the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) issued an order against N26 Bank GmbH to take appropriate internal safety measures and to comply with general Customer Due Diligence obligations. Moreover, N26 Bank GmbH has to ensure the existence of an adequate personnel and technical-organisational equipment in order to comply with its obligations under money laundering law. The decision became legal on May 20, 2019.

According to Financial Supervisory Authority of Norway; February 27, 2023: On February 08, 2023, the Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa issued a warning against Binanfx. Binanfx was not authorized to offer investment services in Italy.

According to Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores de España; February 22, 2023: On February 13, 2023, the Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa issued a warning against Binanfx. Binanfx was not authorized to offer investment services in Italy.

According to International Organization of Securities Commissions; February 17, 2023: On February 17, 2023, the International Organization of Securities Commissions placed N 26 Pty Ltd on a list of unauthorized entities following an order issued by the Italian Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa.

According to Italy Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa; February 13, 2023: On February 08, 2023, the Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa ordered the black-out of Binanfx and its websites, www.binanfx.com and https://account.binanfx.com, for offering financial services illegally.

According to Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores de España; February 01, 2023: On January 19, 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority of the United Kingdom issued a warning against Binanfx. Binanfx was not authorized to offer investment services in the United Kingdom.

According to Italy Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa; January 23, 2023: On January 23, 2023, the Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa placed Binakfx on a list of unauthorized entities following a warning from Financial Conduct Authority of United Kingdom. According to the source, the company and its website offered financial services without the required authorization.

According to Financial Supervision Authority of Estonia and the Slovene Securities Market Agency; January 20, 2023: On January 20, 2023, the Financial Supervision Authority of Estonia placed Binanfx on an unauthorized companies list following a warning issued by the Financial Conduct Authority of the United Kingdom.

According to United Kingdom Financial Conduct Authority, the International Organization of Securities Commissions, the Financial Supervisory of Norway, the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority, the Netherlands Authority for the Financial Markets, the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority and the Financial Supervisory Authority of Finland; January 19, 2023: On January 19, 2023, Binanfx has been providing financial services or products in the United Kingdom without appropriate authorization by FCA.

Abdul Rahman Yasin was born on 10 April 1960.

On December 31, 2020, the United Kingdom under the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office added ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN under its sanctions list. 

On November 24, 2016, the Trinidad and Tobago Financial Intelligence Unit listed ABDUL RAHMAN on its Targeted Financial Sanctions List.

On March 17, 2016, ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN was added to the Indonesian Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Center Suspected Terrorists and Terrorist Organizations list.

On October 17, 2001, the United Nations Security Council imposed sanctions on ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN for being associated with Al-Qaida. Yasin directly assisted terrorist mastermind Ramzi Ahmed Yousef in carrying out the February 26, 1993, World Trade Center bombing in New York City. Yasin fled the United States immediately after the bombing to avoid arrest. He was indicted in the United States for his role in the World Trade Center bombing. He is wanted for his alleged participation in the terrorist bombing of the World Trade Center, New York City, on February 26, 1993, which resulted in six deaths, the wounding of numerous individuals, and the significant destruction of property and commerce.

On October 17, 2001, ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN was added to Argentina Registro Público de Personas y Entidades Vinculadas a Actos de Terrorismo y su Financiamiento-Sanctions List.

Abdul Rahman Yasin has been added to the sanctions Switzerland's State Secretariat for Economic Affairs under the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaeda regime.

Abdul Rahman Yasin has been added to the European Union Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 866/2003 imposing specific restrictive measures against persons and entities associated with Usama bin Laden, the Al-Qaida network and the Taliban.

Abdul Rahman YASIN has been added to the New Zealand Police List - Designated terrorist entity pursuant to UNSC 1267/1989/2253.

The Rewards For Justice Program, United States Department of State, is offering a reward of up to USD 25,000,000 for information leading directly to the apprehension or conviction of Abdul Rahman Yasin.

Abdul Yasin was born in 1960 in Bloomington, Ind., where his Iraqi father was a graduate student, and grew up in Baghdad. He returned to the United States in the early 1990's, to live with his mother and a brother who were living in Jersey City. It was then that he met Ramzi Yousef. Yousef recruited Yasin for the plot to blow up the World Trade Center. Mr. Yasin helped mix the chemicals used in the blast, at one point severely burning his leg. 

Abdul Yasin lived with several of the WTC conspirators at 34 Kensington Ave in Jersey City. The FBI initially detained Mr. Yasin after the attack and then released him. After it realized its error, the FBI placed Abdul Yasin on the list of "Most Wanted" terrorists, but it was too late. On the evening of March 5th, Yasin departed the United States on a Royal Jordanian Airlines flight. The FBI believes that Yasin flew to Jordan and then drove twelve hours to Baghdad, where he has relatives. 

A reporter for ABC News spotted Yasin in Baghdad in 1994 and reported that he was operating freely. A neighbor told the reporter that Yasin was working for the Iraqi government. Documents recovered from postwar Iraq indicate that Yasin received no only safe haven in Iraq, but also funding from the former Iraqi regime. In an interview with the CBS News program "60 Minutes" in June 2002, Mr. Yasin admitted his involvement in the World Trade Center bombing and expressed regret for what he had done. "I'm very sorry for what happened," he said. "I don't know what to do to make it up." Abdul Rahman Yasin is still at large. The United States Department of State is offering a reward of up to $5 million for information leading directly to his apprehension or conviction. 

Yasin is believed to still be in Iraq.

Yousef and Yasin drove a van full of explosives into the basement of the World Trade Center, killing six people and wounding over a thousand. Yasin fled the United States immediately after the bombing to avoid arrest. After the bombing, law enforcement officials obtained evidence which led to the indictment and arrest of several suspected terrorists involved in the bombing, including Yasin. Yasin was born in the United States, moved to Iraq during the 1960s, and returned to the U.S. in the fall of 1992. He possesses a U.S. passport.

Karachi Police seized 20,000 litres of crude oil hidden in the secret parts of a dumper at Shah Latif area of the provincial capital. The accused was concealing and transporting crude oil in a sand and gravel load dumper. He had secretly built a tank in the dumper, during the search 20,000 litres of crude oil was found.

row.profile_notes:
According to ilgiorno.it; September 23, 2015: In September 2015, Giampiero Fiorani was sent on trial by the Prosecutors of Lodi, for subtraction fraudulent payment of taxes. According to the authorities, he transferred the two houses that he owned to his relatives without paying taxes.

According to ilgiorno.it; November 09, 2012: In November 2012 Giampiero Fiorani, former Head of Banca Popolare di Lodi, was sentenced by the Court of Appeal of Nice, to one year of imprisonment and a fine of EUR 300.000 euros for money laundering. The facts dates back in 2003, when the former banker bought for 3 million euro a seaside villa in Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, one of the most exclusive French Riviera. The operation was carried out through the company Liberty, owned in equal parts by two acquaintances of Fiorani. In 2006, Fiorani acquired 45% of the company from one of the two owners and few months later, he sold it to a real estate agent in Monaco.

According to ilfattoquotidiano.it; May 28, 2012: On May 28, 2011 Giampiero Fiorani, was sentenced, to one year and eight months of imprisonment for inside trading and embezzlement in the process called “Antonveneta”. One year later, on May 28, 2012 the sentence was reduced on appeal to one year.

row.profile_notes: Description: On March 1, 1968, The New York State Legislature created the Metropolitan Transportation Authority to oversee transportation operations in 12 counties. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority is the public benefit corporation of the State of New York responsible for an integrated mass transportation system for the City of New York and Dutchess, Nassau, Orange, Putnam, Rockland, Suffolk and Westchester counties. The statutory purposes set forth in the MTA enabling act are: the continuance, further development and improvement of commuter transportation and other services related thereto within the metropolitan commuter transportation district, including but not limited to such transportation by railroad, omnibus, marine and air, in accordance with the provisions of this title. It is governed by a 23-member Board of Directors, whose members are appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the State Senate.

row.position_or_allegation: Unauthorized by Banque de France to provide financial services - September 26, 2022.
row.details: enforcement: Unauthorized/Fraud | FR- Banque De France | France || Unauthorized/Fraud | INT-International Organization of Securities Commissions | N/A || Unauthorized/Fraud | UK-Financial Conduct Authority - Unauthorized Firms/Individuals | United Kingdom
row.profile_notes:
According to Banque de France; September 26, 2022: On September 26, 2022, the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR) updated its black list of the entities not authorized to offer loans, savings accounts, payment services or insurance contracts. The website www.starlingcredit.com has been added to this list.

According to Italian Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa; September 12, 2022: On September 12, 2022, the Italian Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa placed Starling Credit on a list of unauthorized entities following a warning issued by the Financial Conduct Authority of the United Kingdom.

According to Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores de España; August 24, 2022: On August 19, 2022, Starling Credit (Clone) is not authorized by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier Luxembourg to provide provide financial services. This entity is fraudulently using the name of an authorized firm to appear authorized. Starling Credit has no association with the clone entity.

According to Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier Luxembourg, the Netherlands Authority for the Financial Markets, the Slovene Securities Market Agency and the Financial Supervisory Authority of Denmark; August 19, 2022: On August 19, 2022, the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier Luxembourg issued a warning against Starling Credit. Starling Credit does not have the authorization to provide investment or financial services in or from Luxembourg.

According to United Kingdom Financial Conduct Authority, the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority, International Organization of Securities Commissions and the Netherlands Authority for the Financial Markets; August 16, 2022: On August 16, 2022, Starling Credit (Clone) is not an authorized finance company in the United Kingdomand is not permitted to provide financial services in the United Kingdom, this entity is using the name of an authorized firm to defraud consumers. Almost all firms and individuals carrying out financial services activities in the United Kingdom have to be authorised or registered by the FCA. This firm is not authorised or registered by the FCA, but has been targeting people in the United Kingdom, claiming to be an authorised firm. They may use the name of the genuine firm, the firm reference number (FRN) FCA have given the authorised firm or other details. Starling Credit (Clone) is not authorized by the FCA to provide financial services. This entity is fraudulently using the name of an authorized firm to appear authorized. Starling Bank Limited has no association with the Clone entity.

row.position_or_allegation: Fined GBP 28,959,426 for financial crime failings - September 27, 2024.
row.details: enforcement: Disciplined/Financial Crimes | UK-Financial Conduct Authority | United Kingdom
row.profile_notes: According to the United Kingdom-Financial Conduct Authority; September 27, 2024: The Authority hereby imposes on Starling Bank Limited (“Starling”) a financial penalty of GBP 28,959,426 pursuant to section 206 of the Act. Starling agreed to resolve this matter and qualified for a 30% (stage 1) discount under the Authority’s executive settlement procedures. Were it not for this discount, the Authority would have imposed a financial penalty of GBP 40,959,426 on Starling. Starling grew quickly, from approximately 43,000 customers in 2017 to 3.6 million in 2023. However, measures to tackle financial crime did not keep pace with its growth. When the FCA reviewed financial crime controls at challenger banks in 2021, it identified serious concerns with the anti-money laundering and sanctions framework in place at Starling. The bank agreed to a requirement restricting it from opening new accounts for high-risk customers until this improved. Starling failed to comply and opened over 54,000 accounts for 49,000 high-risk customers between September 2021 and November 2023. In January 2023, Starling became aware that its automated screening system had, since 2017, only been screening customers against a fraction of the full list of those subject to financial sanctions. A subsequent internal review identified systemic issues in its financial sanctions framework. Starling has since reported multiple potential breaches of financial sanctions to the relevant authorities.

row.details: enforcement: Bank Fraud/Disciplined | US-U.S. FDIC Temporary Order to Cease and Desist | United States || Disciplined/Bank Fraud | US-U.S. FDIC Order to Cease and Desist | United States || Bank Fraud/Disciplined | US-U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation | United States || Disciplined/Bank Fraud | US-Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division | United States
row.relationships: Financial Pacific Leasing (AffiliatedCompany; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; May 10, 2021: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation announced a settlement with Umpqua Bank for engaging in unfair and deceptive practices, in violation of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act (Section 5). Umpqua Bank stipulated to the issuance of an Order to Pay Civil Money Penalty (CMP) in the amount of USD 1,800,000.

The FDIC determined that Umpqua Bank engaged in Section 5 violations related to collection practices involving commercial equipment financing through its wholly owned subsidiary, Financial Pacific Leasing, Inc.. The FDIC determined that FinPac’s collection fee practices were unfair and deceptive. Specifically, FinPac charged various undisclosed collection fees to borrowers whose accounts were past due, such as collection call and letter fees and third-party collection fees.

The FDIC also determined that certain collection practices at FinPac were unfair and deceptive. FinPac engaged in excessive and sequential collection calls to customers, even when customers requested that FinPac stop these calls. FinPac also disclosed information about the customers’ debts to third parties. Lastly, FinPac advised borrowers FinPac would report delinquencies on commercial debt to the consumer reporting agencies, when its policy and practice was not to report such delinquencies to the consumer reporting agencies. Umpqua Bank agreed to the issuance of the Order without admitting or denying these violations. In addition, the Bank voluntarily paid restitution totaling approximately USD 1,628,000 to the 16,902 customers who were charged the undisclosed collection fees.

According to U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; May 06, 2021; Umpqua Bank ordered to pay penalty of USD 1,800,000 for engaged in violations of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act. 

According to U.S. FDIC Temporary Order to Cease and Desist and U.S. Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division; September 27, 2010: The Cease and Desist order against Sterling Savings Bank has been terminated.

According to the U.S. FDIC Order to Cease and Desist and U.S. Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division; October 9, 2009: Cease and desist order issued against Sterling Savings Bank from the following unsafe and unsound banking practices, as more fully set forth in the joint FDIC and WDFI Report of Visitation dated June 29, 2009. The FDIC and the WDFI considered the matter and determined that they had reason to believe that the Bank had engaged in unsafe or unsound banking practices and violations of law and/or regulations. Sterling Savings Bank  failed to maintain the minimum capital ratio, failed to submit an acceptable capital plan and failed to implement or adhere to a capital plan to which the Regional Director and the Director of Banks have taken no written objection.

According to U.S. Department of Justice, United States Attorney - District of New Jersey and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency; December 16, 2022: On December 16, 2022, A complaint was filed against Purdue Pharma Technologies Inc for discharging hazardous substances into the Lower Passaic River. The proposed consent decree seeks to hold the parties accountable for their share of the total cost of cleaning up this stretch of the river.

EPA expects to use the settlement funds to support ongoing efforts to clean up the site, specifically the lower 8.3 miles and the upper 9 miles which make up the entire 17-mile Lower Passaic River Study Area. In addition to the proposed consent decree, EPA has reached several related agreements, including one whereby many parties investigated the 17-mile Lower Passaic River, another whereby Occidental Chemical Corporation, a potentially responsible party, is designing the cleanup chosen for the lower 8.3 miles, and several cost recovery agreements that resulted in payments to EPA of millions of dollars.

According to the U.S. North Carolina Attorney General; May 15, 2018: A lawsuit was filed against Purdue Pharma Technologies Inc for allegedly using a campaign of misrepresentations and omissions about the use of opioids to doctors and consumers in order to increase prescriptions and opioid use, including false statements about the addictive nature of opioids and omissions of the severe risks posed by taking opioids. 

The opioid distributors allegedly shipped inordinately high volumes of opioids to customers in Florida and failed to report these suspicious orders of opioids, thereby fueling widespread diversion of opioids throughout the state. In the complaint filed the defendants’ actions violated the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, the Florida RICO Act, and violated common law public nuisance and negligence.

row.profile_notes:
According to United States - Colorado Attorney General and the Department of Law, United States - Vermont Attorney General, United States - New York State Attorney General, United States - Massachusetts Attorney General, United States - Connecticut Attorney General, United States - Virginia Attorney General, United States - Tennessee Attorney General, United States - Texas Attorney General, United States - Delaware Attorney General and the Department of Justice, United States - California Attorney General, United States - Pennsylvania Attorney General, United States - Montana Attorney General and United States - Florida Attorney General; January 23, 2025: Published on that date, settlement reached USD 7,400,000,000 against Purdue Pharma for creating the opioid crisis. Purdue invented, manufactured, and aggressively marketed opioids for decades, fueling waves of addiction and overdose deaths across the country. The settlement ends the Sacklers’ control of Purdue and their ability to sell opioids in the United States. Purdue will continue to be overseen by a monitor and will be prevented from lobbying or marketing opioids under the settlement. A significant amount of the settlement funds will be distributed in the first three years, with the Sacklers paying USD 1,500,000,000 and Purdue paying nearly USD 900,000,000 in the first payment, followed by USD 500,000,000 after one year, an additional $500 million after two years, and USD 400,000 after three years.

Colorado will receive approximately USD 81,000,000 from the settlement;
Vermont will receive USD 22,000,000;
New York will receive USD 250,000,000 from the settlement; 
Massachusetts will receive USD 90,000,000;
Florida will receive between USD 233,370,000 - 325,930,000;
Connecticut will receive approximately USD 64,000,000 from the settlement; 
Virginia will receive approximately USD 107,400,000 from the settlement; 
Tennessee will receive more than USD 90,000,000; 
Delaware will receive over USD 27,000,000;
California expected to receive hundreds of millions of dollars;
Pennsylvania will receive up to USD 212,000,000 from the settlement;
Montana will receive nearly USD 4,000,000.

According to United States - Department of Justice; October 21, 2020: On October 21, 2020, Purdue Pharma pleaded guilty to three felony counts for defrauding the United States and violating the Anti-Kickback Statute from 2009 to 2017.  In addition to agreeing to plead guilty to these three felonies counts, the company has agreed to a USD 3,544,000,000, criminal fine and a USD 2,000,000,000 criminal forfeiture amount.  Further, to resolve its civil liability, Purdue Pharma has agreed to USD 2,800,000,000 in damages to the United States.  The company is in bankruptcy, so the corporate resolution is subject to the bankruptcy court’s approval.  If approved, this will be a corporate settlement totaling more than USD 8,300,000,000.  Additionally, members of the Sackler family have agreed to pay USD 225,000,000,000 in a civil settlement that will provide civil releases only.

According to theguardian.com; August 19, 2020: Published on that date, A Department of Justice internal memorandum obtained that Purdue Pharma have committed wire fraud and money laundering crimes to boost sales of its billion-dollar OxyContin opioid.

According to United States - California Attorney General; October 03, 2019: On October 03, 2019, an amended complaint lawsuit against filed against Purdue Pharma, adding eight additional members of the Sackler family. In the lawsuit, it is alleged that Purdue misleadingly introduced OxyContin into the market as a safe and effective treatment for chronic, non-cancer pain. As early as February 1997, Purdue and certain of the Sackler defendants knew that oxycodone-containing drugs like OxyContin were among the most abused opioids in the United States. Yet, between 1996 and 2002, Purdue more than doubled its sales force, and sales rose from approximately USD 48,000,000 to nearly USD 2,000,000,000  in 2002. These sales were made by representatives falsely promoting OxyContin as a drug that was neither addictive nor subject to withdrawal symptoms, while minimizing its potential for abuse and addiction. By March 2000, Purdue was aware of specific reports made to the company about the abuse and diversion of OxyContin occurring in communities across the United States. In fact, in 2007, Purdue and a number of its executives pleaded guilty to felony misbranding of OxyContin, admitting that they illegally promoted OxyContin. Purdue agreed to pay over USD 600,000,000 in criminal and civil penalties, fines, and forfeitures.

Purdue continued its deceptive marketing and promoting of OxyContin. Their revenues amounted to USD 3,000,000,000  in 2010, and as much as USD 1,800,000,000 as recently as 2017. The lawsuit further alleges that as part of its aggressive deceptive marketing campaign, Purdue distributed literature and other materials that misrepresented the safety of its opioid products to healthcare professionals and patients in California and elsewhere. Purdue sales representatives further pushed physicians to prescribe opioids to “trusted” patients, and implied that healthcare professionals could screen out potential addicts through urine tests and patient contracts. In addition to the amended complaint, Attorney General also joined a coalition of 23 attorneys general and formally opposed Purdue Pharma’s request to make USD 38,000,000 in bonus, incentive, and other payments to employees.

According to the United States - Rhode Island Attorney General, United States - Virginia Attorney General and United States - Pennsylvania Attorney General; September 11, 2019: On September 11, 2019, The State of Rhode Island, by and through its Attorney General, brings this action pursuant to his statutory and common law authority to redress Richard S. Sacker's, Jonathan D. Sackler's, Mortimer D.A. Sackler's, Kathe A. Sackler's, Ilene Sackler Lefcourt's, David A. Sackler's, and Beverly Sackler's (together, the Sacklers) campaign to unlawfully promote and distribute opioids in Rhode Island through their control and use of Purdue Pharma, L.P.'s, Purdue Pharma Inc.'s, the Purdue Frederick Company ( together, Purdue), and the fraudulent transfer of funds generated from such sales to the Sacklers and Prescription opioid are dangerous drugs that have harmed the public health, safety and welfare affecting every community in our State causing the epidemic of opioid addiction and death.

Rhode Island government committed to continuing to aggressively pursue our claims against Purdue Pharma and the Sacklers. On September 11, 2019, filed a complaint against additional members of the Sackler family for the role that they played in the distribution of these highly addictive opioids in Rhode Island.

According to United States - Rhode Island Attorney General; August 16, 2019: Published on that date, The Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma Inc. for pharma trafficking. The lawsuit alleges that defendant opioid manufacturers and distributors knowingly misrepresented the risk posed by prescription opioids in order expand their use and drive-up profits. It is also alleged that, in particular, opioid distributors disregarded obligations to identify suspicious orders and customers, allowing for and failing to stop the diversion of opioids within and to Rhode Island.

According to United States - Arizona Attorney General; July 31, 2019: On July 31, 2019, Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma Inc. And others for engaging in deceptive and misleading marketing to push opioids in violation of a 2007 judgment obtained by the Arizona Attorney General’s Office for violating the state’s Consumer Fraud Act.

The defendants allegedly disregarded the judgment and continued to disseminate false, misleading, or unbalanced information through Purdue’s sales representatives, advertising materials, and websites. The State also alleges that they violated the judgment by improperly marketing prescription opioids, including OxyContin, through seemingly independent nonprofits that were paid millions of dollars by Purdue to promote prescription opioids.

According to United States - Nevada Attorney General; June 17, 2019: On June 17, 2019, lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma Inc. and others for violations of the Nevada Deceptive Trade Practices Act.

The lawsuit alleges that the manufacturers, distributors, pharmacies, and individuals created an ecosystem of addiction with deadly consequences to the state and its residents for their own profit. Through a systematic marketing campaign, sham “medical” organizations, funded experts, and other shameful tactics, the defendant’s peddled false science designed to demonstrate that opioids were a safe, non-addictive treatment for pain. The defendants furthered their wrongful conduct by encouraging doctors to treat addiction with more opioids and intensify the epidemic they created. Even when opioid deaths skyrocketed, the defendants simply redesigned their marketing campaign to continue to reap profits at the expense of Nevadans. Legal causes of action include violations of Nevada’s Deceptive Trade Practices Act, False Claims Act, Racketeering Act, negligence, and public nuisance.

The Complaint lists over 40 defendants. Manufacturer defendants include Purdue Pharma Inc. Manufacturer Defendants have packaged, distributed, supplied, sold, placed into the stream of commerce, labeled, described, marketed, advertised, promoted and purported to warn or purported to inform prescribers and users regarding the benefits and risks associated with the use of the prescription opioid drugs. 

According to United States - Hawaii Attorney General, United States - Maine Attorney General, United States - California Attorney General and United States - District of Columbia Attorney General; June 03, 2019: Published on that date, Purdue Pharma L.P., Purdue Pharma Inc. (Purdue), certain of its affiliates, and Dr. Richard S. Sackler was sued for unlawful practices in the marketing, sale, and distribution of opioids. The lawsuit alleges that Purdue’s illegal and misleading marketing and sales practices played a major role in contributing to the nationwide opioid crisis. It further alleges that Purdue created a public nuisance through its marketing and sale of opioids and misled healthcare professionals and patients about the addictive nature of opioids and their potential for abuse and diversion.

According to United States - Pennsylvania Attorney General, United States - Iowa Attorney General, United States - Maryland Attorney General, United States - Minnesota Attorney General, United States - Oregon Department of Justice Office of the Attorney General and United States - Kansas Attorney General; May 2019: In May 2019, a lawsuit was filed against Purdue Pharma, the creator of prescription painkiller OxyContin, accusing the company of a multi-faceted, illegal effort to market OxyContin in Pennsylvania. Shapiro’s suit is the first to specifically detail Purdue’s barrage of sales representatives targeting Pennsylvania doctors as a key facet of their campaign to push addictive opioids on Pennsylvanians.

The lawsuit alleges that Purdue launched an illegal marketing campaign of deception targeting Pennsylvania doctors and patients to change attitudes, practices, and the culture surrounding pain management. Some of the most egregious components of the campaign include Purdue deployed their highly trained sales staff to blanket Pennsylvania, making sales calls and in-person visits to physicians, totaling more than half a million visits in Pennsylvania alone, an amount second to only California. Purdue targeted Pennsylvania doctors with suspicious prescribing activity and would invest more sales force and marketing to get those doctors to prescribe even more OxyContin – sometimes resulting in as much as a 500% increase in OxyContin prescriptions by one office alone. Purdue misinformed doctors and pharmacists about the addictive nature of OxyContin and used industry thought leaders and in-house marketing literature to dispel the facts about the drug. As the opioid epidemic grew, Purdue created “pseudo-addiction,” a Purdue-conjured disease that showed similar equities as addiction but was to be treated, according to Purdue, with additional opioids. The Office of Attorney General is demanding that the Court issue an order preventing Purdue and anyone associated with Purdue’s misconduct from continuing to engage in these same deceptive tactics. 

According to United States - Illinois Attorney General; April 8, 2019: On April 8, 2019, Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma L.P. and Purdue Pharma Inc. over its deceptive marketing practices designed to significantly increase prescriptions issued for opioids.

Between 2008 and 2017, Purdue dispatched sales representatives to Illinois hundreds of thousands of times. Raoul alleged Purdue also funded third-party publications under the guise of educational materials to promote opioids and downplay their risks, using terms like “pseudo addiction.” Sales representatives informed doctors and patients that the risks could be controlled. Despite knowing that its opioid painkillers were dangerous and being misused and diverted, Purdue allegedly targeted doctors with addicted patients and whose patients were diverting drugs for unlawful use. Raoul alleged that Purdue’s tactics tripled prescriptions of its opioids in Illinois.

According to United States - New York State Attorney General; March 28, 2019: Published on that date, The lawsuit filed Purdue Pharma Inc. against for engaging in healthcare fraud. 

Pursuant to Executive Law § 63(12), From manufacturing, distributing, selling, or marketing opioids within the State unless it complies with heightened, independently monitored safeguards against the recurrence of its fraudulent, illegal, and/or unlawful practices, which are to be set forth in a compliance plan reviewed and approved by Plaintiff and the Court.  Pursuant to Executive Law § 63(12), Pay restitution and damages for its fraudulent and/or illegal practices that violated that statute and caused compensable injuries to Plaintiff or any other person; and disgorge all profits it wrongfully obtained as a result of its fraudulent and/or illegal practices in violation of that statute.

According to United States - Utah Attorney General; January 30, 2019: Published on that date, The Utah Attorney General’s Office filed an administrative action against Purdue Pharma Inc. and others as part of the State’s efforts to hold accountable the opioid companies and individuals that created and fueled the opioid epidemic throughout Utah.

In the filing, under Utah Code, the Division of Consumer Protection of the Department of Commerce issued an administrative action, in the form of a citation, against the defendants alleging violations of the Utah Consumer Sales Practices Act. An administrative proceeding allows the State to seek to prove its claims and obtain a judgment, injunctive relief, and civil penalties more promptly than state district court proceedings. Based on evidence that has emerged over 2018, this administrative action alleges that not only Purdue, but two of its owners also participated in Purdue’s fraudulent conduct.

According to United States - Connecticut Attorney General; December 20, 2018: Published on that date, the lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma Inc. and other affiliates for alleging that they designed, financed and waged a pervasive and aggressive campaign to mislead doctors and patients, claiming that prescription opioid medications manufactured and marketed by the company were safe and effective and strategically downplaying risks of addiction that they knew were inherent in their opioid products.

The state alleges that Purdue misinformed patients and doctors to get more and more people taking its premier opioid drug, OxyContin, and its two other opioid medications, Hysingla and Butrans. Purdue allegedly led patients and doctors to believe that opioids were safe to treat even minor pain, and that patients could and should take higher and more dangerous doses. The state alleges that Purdue sent sales representatives to doctors' offices, clinics, pharmacies and hospitals in Connecticut to make deceptive sales pitches about opioid drugs; rewarded high-prescribing doctors with attention, meals, gifts and money; and awarded prizes and bonuses to sales representatives who generated the most opioid prescriptions. In Connecticut, 1038 people died of accidental drug overdoses in 2017, the vast majority from opioid-related overdoses. The Connecticut Office of the Chief Medical Examiner has projected that 1030 more people will die of overdoses in 2018. From 2013 to 2016, Connecticut experienced a fourfold increase in deaths from prescription opioid overdoses, and the estimated economic cost of the opioid epidemic in Connecticut in 2016 was USD 10,270,000,000.

According to United States - Florida Attorney General-Sixth Judicial Circuit: November 16, 2018: Published on that date, an amended complaint was filed against opioid manufacturers and distributors including Purdue Pharma Inc. Allegedly, defendants deceptively, unfairly, and unconscionably sought to convince prescribers and patients that opioids are safe, rarely addictive, and necessary for treating a wide range of common ailments. Defendants spread these myths knowing that opioids create physical dependency within days or weeks; that withdrawal from prescription opioids can be agonizing; that long-term and high-dose opioid use is particularly likely to lead to addiction; and that high doses of opioids can be fatal. Defendants at all levels of the supply chain manufacturers, distributors, and chain pharmacies continued selling opioids in Florida even though they knew or should have known that the drugs were being diverted and misused for non-medical purposes. Defendants had duties to identify and stop suspicious orders and purchases, and to put in place reasonable policies to safeguard against diversion.

According to United States - Oregon Department of Justice Office of the Attorney General; September 13, 2018: Published on that date, the complaint alleges on Purdue Pharma Inc and Purdue deceptively marketed OxyContin to Oregon seniors, misrepresented the risks and benefits of the drug, and lied to the Oregon Board of Pharmacy, all to maximize Purdue’s profits. It states that over the last decade Purdue has engaged in a pattern of racketeering and misleading activity in Oregon.

he complaint, filed in Multnomah Circuit Court, details how Purdue’s conduct violated an agreed upon stipulated 2007 Oregon judgment resulting from an earlier investigation of its unlawful practices, as well as four distinct Oregon laws: The Unlawful Trade Practices Act, the Elderly Persons and Persons with Disabilities Abuse Prevention Act, the False Claims Act and the Oregon Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act.

According to United States - Rhode Island Attorney General and United States - Virginia Attorney General; June 2018: On June 25, 2018, A civil lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma Inc., for prescription opioid manufacturers and distributors over their alleged campaign of unfairly, deceptively, and fraudulently marketing and promoting opioids in Rhode Island.

According to the Complaint, distributors persistently disregarded their obligations to identify suspicious orders and customers, facilitating and failing to stop the diversion of opioids within and to Rhode Island. Rhode Island's Medicaid program spent more than USD 6,000,000 to pay for prescriptions of Purdue-branded opioids, along with additional funds for Purdue's generic opioids and for the costs of providing and using opioids long-term to treat chronic pain.

According to United States - Florida Attorney General, United States - North Carolina Attorney General, United States - North Dakota Attorney General and United States - Texas Attorney General; May 15, 2018: Published on that date, a lawsuit was filed against Purdue Pharma Inc., for allegedly using a campaign of misrepresentations and omissions about the use of opioids to doctors and consumers in order to increase prescriptions and opioid use, including false statements about the addictive nature of opioids and omissions of the severe risks posed by taking opioids. 

The opioid distributors allegedly shipped inordinately high volumes of opioids to customers in Florida and failed to report these suspicious orders of opioids, thereby fueling widespread diversion of opioids throughout the state. In the complaint filed the defendants’ actions violated the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, the Florida RICO Act, and violated common law public nuisance and negligence.

According to United States - South Dakota Attorney General; March 14, 2018: On March 14, 2018, Attorney General announced that his office has filed a civil lawsuit in South Dakota State Circuit Court against prescription drug manufactures Purdue, Endo and Janssen for deceptive marketing and sale of prescription opioids.

According to United States - Delaware Attorney General and the Department of Justice; January 19, 2018: On January 19, 2018, A lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma Inc for engaging in false, deceptive and unfair marketing of prescription opioids.

Purdue Pharma Inc engaged, and continue to engage, in a massive marketing campaign to misstate and conceal the risks of treating chronic pain with opioids. Although manufacturers are prohibited from marketing opioids through misstatements or omissions of material facts, Manufacturer Defendants nonetheless disseminated misstatements through multiple channels. This campaign includes websites, promotional materials, conferences, guidelines for doctors, and other vehicles.

Defendant Purdue Pharma Inc. is a corporation organized and existing under the laws of New York State with its principal place of business located in Stamford, Connecticut. During all relevant times, Purdue Pharma Inc. has manufactured and distributed substantial amounts of prescription opioids that have been and continue to be sold in Delaware. Purdue Pharma Inc. has engaged in consensual commercial dealings with Delaware and its citizens and has purposefully availed itself of the advantages of conducting business with and within Delaware.  

According to United States - Washington Attorney General: September 28, 2017: Published on that date, A lawsuit filed against OxyContin maker Purdue Pharma, Inc for fueling the opioid epidemic in Washington state, embarking on a massive deceptive marketing campaign and convincing doctors and the public that their drugs are effective for treating chronic pain and have a low risk of addiction, contrary to overwhelming evidence. This deceptive marketing resulted in the deaths of Washingtonians and devastation to Washington families. The City of Seattle filed a separate lawsuit against Purdue.

The lawsuit contends Purdue conducted an uncontrolled experiment on the American public without any reliable clinical evidence that opioids are effective at treating chronic pain. To doctors and patients, Purdue consistently downplayed the risks of addiction from long-term use and deceptively represented opioids as safe for treating long-term chronic pain.

According to United States - New Jersey Bureau of Securities; October 31, 2017: On October 31, 2017, A lawsuit filed against  Purdue Pharma L.P and its co defendants Purdue Pharma Inc. and Purdue Frederick Company alleging a direct link between New Jersey’s opioid crisis and a push by Purdue to boost profits by deceptively marketing addictive medications and exploiting vulnerable new markets, such as the elderly and the “opioid-naïve. The lawsuit charges Purdue with widespread deception about the risks and benefits of these dangerously addictive pain medications.

According to United States - New Mexico Attorney General: September 7, 2017: On September 7, 2017, Attorney General Hector Balderas announced that he has brought a lawsuit on behalf of the State of New Mexico against the country’s largest manufacturers and wholesale distributors of opioids, a crucial first step toward holding these companies responsible for flooding New Mexico’s communities with prescription opioids and fueling the opioid epidemic by putting profits over people. The State of New Mexico is filing suit against five of the largest manufacturers of prescription opioids and their related companies and against the country’s three largest wholesale drug distributors. The manufacturing companies pushed highly addictive, dangerous opioids, falsely representing to doctors that patients would only rarely succumb to drug addiction, while the distributors breached their legal duties to monitor, detect, investigate, refuse and report suspicious orders of prescription opioids.

Complaint against Defendants Purdue Pharma L.P., Purdue Pharma, Inc., The Purdue Frederick Company, Inc., Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, LTD., Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc., Cephalon, Inc., Johnson & Johnson, Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Ortho-McNeil-Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. n/k/a Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Janssen Pharmaceutica Inc. n/k/a Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Endo Health Solutions Inc., Endo Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Allergan PLC f/k/a Actavis PLS, Watson Pharmaceuticals, Inc. n/k/a Actavis, Inc., Watson Laboratories, Inc., Actavis, LLC, Actavis Pharma, Inc. f/k/a Watson Pharma, Inc., McKesson Corporation, Cardinal Health, Inc., Cardinal Health 105, LLC, Cardinal Health 108, LLC, Cardinal Health 110, LLC, Cardinal Health 200, LLC, Cardinal Health 414, LLC, Cardinal Health Pharmacy Services, LLC, and AmerisourceBergen Drug Corporation and alleges, upon information and belief, as follows.

Opioid manufacturers, including Defendants Endo Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and Purdue Pharma L.P., have entered into settlement agreements with public entities that prohibit them from making many of the misrepresentations identified in this Complaint. Yet even afterward, each Manufacturer Defendant continued to misrepresent the risks and benefits of longterm opioid use in New Mexico and continues to fail to correct its past misrepresentations.
