According to United States Colorado Attorney General and the Department of Law, United States New York State Attorney General, United States Idaho Attorney General, United States Minnesota Attorney General, United States Iowa Attorney General, United States Pennsylvania Attorney General, United States Nevada Attorney General,  United States Virginia Attorney General, United States Hawaii Attorney General, United States Maine Attorney General; United States Wisconsin Department of Justice - Office of the Attorney General and United States Massachusetts Attorney General; July, 2021: On July 08, 2021, Resolution of the State’s lawsuit filed against the Sackler family and the company they controlled, Purdue Pharma, manufacturer of the blockbuster opioid drug Oxycontin and a major contributor to the deadly opioid crisis across America. The resolution of lawsuit against Purdue and the Sacklers, will make public tens of millions of documents related to Purdue’s role in the deadly opioid crisis. It also requires the Sacklers personally to pay USD 4,325,000,000 over nine years for prevention, treatment, and recovery efforts in communities across the country.

According to United States Attorney - District of Vermont, United States - Department of Health & Human Services, United States - Department of Justice and United States Attorney - District of New Jersey; November 24, 2020: On November 24, 2020, Opioid company Purdue Pharma LP, pleaded guilty in federal court to conspiracies to defraud the United States and to violate the Anti-Kickback Statute. Purdue pleaded guilty to an Information charging it with three felony offenses, one count of dual-object conspiracy to defraud the United States and to violate the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and two counts of conspiracy to violate the Federal Anti-Kickback Statute.

From May 2007 to March 2017, Purdue conspired to defraud the United States by impeding the lawful function of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). The misleading information comprised prescription data that included prescriptions written by doctors that Purdue had good reason to believe were engaged in diversion. The conspiracy also involved aiding and abetting violations of the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act by facilitating the dispensing of its opioid products, including OxyContin, without a legitimate medical purpose, and thus without lawful prescriptions. Purdue also admitted it conspired to violate the Anti-Kickback Statute, between June 2009 to March 2017, by making payments to two doctors through Purdue’s physician speaker program to induce those doctors to write more prescriptions for Purdue’s opioid products.

According to United States - Maryland Attorney General, United States - Department of Justice, United States - Department of Health & Human Services, United States Attorney - District of New Jersey, United States Attorney - District of Vermont, United States Attorney - District of Maine and United States Attorney - Eastern District of Texas; October 21, 2020: On October 21, 2020 Purdue Pharma LP,  pleaded guilty to conspiracy to defraud the United States and to violate the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and two counts of conspiracy to violate the Federal Anti-Kickback Statute. Purdue has also agreed to a civil settlement in the amount of USD 2,800,000,000 to resolve its civil liability under the False Claims Act. Between June 2009 and March 2017, Purdue made payments to two doctors through Purdue’s doctor speaker program to induce those doctors to write more prescriptions of Purdue’s opioid products.  Similarly, from approximately April 2016 through December 2016, Purdue made payments to Practice Fusion Inc., an electronic health records company, in exchange for referring, recommending, and arranging for the ordering of Purdue’s extended-release opioid products – OxyContin, Butrans, and Hysingla.

According to United States - California Attorney General; October 03, 2019: On October 03, 2019, an amended complaint lawsuit against filed against Purdue Pharma, adding eight additional members of the Sackler family. In the lawsuit, it is alleged that Purdue misleadingly introduced OxyContin into the market as a safe and effective treatment for chronic, non-cancer pain. As early as February 1997, Purdue and certain of the Sackler defendants knew that oxycodone-containing drugs like OxyContin were among the most abused opioids in the United States. Yet, between 1996 and 2002, Purdue more than doubled its sales force, and sales rose from approximately USD 48,000,000 to nearly USD 2,000,000,000 in 2002. These sales were made by representatives falsely promoting OxyContin as a drug that was neither addictive nor subject to withdrawal symptoms, while minimizing its potential for abuse and addiction. By March 2000, Purdue was aware of specific reports made to the company about the abuse and diversion of OxyContin occurring in communities across the United States. In fact, in 2007, Purdue and a number of its executives pleaded guilty to felony misbranding of OxyContin, admitting that they illegally promoted OxyContin. Purdue agreed to pay over USD 600,000,000 in criminal and civil penalties, fines, and forfeitures.

Despite this, Purdue continued its deceptive marketing and promoting of OxyContin. Their revenues amounted to USD 3,000,000,000 in 2010, and as much as USD 1,800,000,000 as recently as 2017. The lawsuit further alleges that as part of its aggressive deceptive marketing campaign, Purdue distributed literature and other materials that misrepresented the safety of its opioid products to healthcare professionals and patients in California and elsewhere. Purdue sales representatives further pushed physicians to prescribe opioids to “trusted” patients, and implied that healthcare professionals could screen out potential addicts through urine tests and patient contracts. In addition to the amended complaint, Attorney General also joined a coalition of 23 attorneys general and formally opposed Purdue Pharma’s request to make USD 38,000,000 in bonus, incentive, and other payments to employees.

According to United States - Rhode Island Attorney General, United States - Virginia Attorney General and United States - Pennsylvania Attorney General; September 11, 2019: On September 11, 2019, The State of Rhode Island, by and through its Attorney General, brings this action pursuant to his statutory and common law authority to redress Richard S. Sacker's, Jonathan D. Sackler's, Mortimer D.A. Sackler's, Kathe A. Sackler's, Ilene Sackler Lefcourt's, David A. Sackler's, and Beverly Sackler's (together, the Sacklers) campaign to unlawfully promote and distribute opioids in Rhode Island through their control and use of Purdue Pharma, L.P.'s, Purdue Pharma Inc.'s, the Purdue Frederick Company ( together, Purdue), and the fraudulent transfer of funds generated from such sales to the Sacklers and Prescription opioid are dangerous drugs that have harmed the public health, safety and welfare affecting every community in our State causing the epidemic of opioid addiction and death.

Rhode Island government committed to continuing to aggressively pursue our claims against Purdue Pharma and the Sacklers. On September 11, 2019, filed a complaint against additional members of the Sackler family for the role that they played in the distribution of these highly addictive opioids in Rhode Island.

According to United States - Rhode Island Attorney General; August 16, 2019: Published on that date, The Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma L.P for pharma trafficking. The lawsuit alleges that defendant opioid manufacturers and distributors knowingly misrepresented the risk posed by prescription opioids in order expand their use and drive-up profits. It is also alleged that, in particular, opioid distributors disregarded obligations to identify suspicious orders and customers, allowing for and failing to stop the diversion of opioids within and to Rhode Island.

According to United States - Arizona Attorney General; July 31, 2019: On July 31, 2019, Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma LP and others for engaging in deceptive and misleading marketing to push opioids in violation of a 2007 judgment obtained by the Arizona Attorney General’s Office for violating the state’s Consumer Fraud Act.

The defendants allegedly disregarded the judgment and continued to disseminate false, misleading, or unbalanced information through Purdue’s sales representatives, advertising materials, and websites. The State also alleges that they violated the judgment by improperly marketing prescription opioids, including OxyContin, through seemingly independent nonprofits that were paid millions of dollars by Purdue to promote prescription opioids.

According to United States - Nevada Attorney General; June 17, 2019: On June 17, 2019, lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma LP and others for violations of the Nevada Deceptive Trade Practices Act.

The lawsuit alleges that the manufacturers, distributors, pharmacies, and individuals created an ecosystem of addiction with deadly consequences to the state and its residents for their own profit. Through a systematic marketing campaign, sham “medical” organizations, funded experts, and other shameful tactics, the defendant’s peddled false science designed to demonstrate that opioids were a safe, non-addictive treatment for pain. The defendants furthered their wrongful conduct by encouraging doctors to treat addiction with more opioids and intensify the epidemic they created. Even when opioid deaths skyrocketed, the defendants simply redesigned their marketing campaign to continue to reap profits at the expense of Nevadans. Legal causes of action include violations of Nevada’s Deceptive Trade Practices Act, False Claims Act, Racketeering Act, negligence, and public nuisance.

The Complaint lists over 40 defendants. Manufacturer defendants include Purdue Pharma LP. Manufacturer Defendants have packaged, distributed, supplied, sold, placed into the stream of commerce, labeled, described, marketed, advertised, promoted and purported to warn or purported to inform prescribers and users regarding the benefits and risks associated with the use of the prescription opioid drugs. 

According to United States - Hawaii Attorney General, United States - Maine Attorney General, United States - California Attorney General and United States - District of Columbia Attorney General; June 03, 2019: Published on that date, Purdue Pharma L.P., Purdue Pharma Inc. (Purdue), certain of its affiliates, and Dr. Richard S. Sackler was sued for unlawful practices in the marketing, sale, and distribution of opioids. The lawsuit alleges that Purdue’s illegal and misleading marketing and sales practices played a major role in contributing to the nationwide opioid crisis. It further alleges that Purdue created a public nuisance through its marketing and sale of opioids and misled healthcare professionals and patients about the addictive nature of opioids and their potential for abuse and diversion.

According to United States - Iowa Attorney General, United States - Maryland Attorney General, United States - Minnesota Attorney General, United States - Oregon Department of Justice Office of the Attorney General and United States - Kansas Attorney General; May 2019: On May 2019,  law suit filed against Purdue Pharma LP for alleging that the drug company engaged in unfair, deceptive and unlawful practices in the marketing of OxyContin, helping fuel the nation’s opioid crisis.

Iowa’s lawsuit, filed in Polk County District Court, seeks restitution and civil penalties under Iowa’s Consumer Fraud Act. It alleges that Purdue, and its related companies Purdue Frederick Co., Purdue Pharmaceuticals and P.F. Laboratories, repeatedly made false and deceptive claims that OxyContin was safe and suitable for a wide range of pain patients. Specifically, the lawsuit alleges that Purdue claimed that OxyContin posed a low risk of addiction; symptoms of addiction were in fact only “pseudoaddiction” indicating the need for more opioids; long-term opioid use improved patients’ quality of life and function; and that opioids were suitable for vulnerable groups, such as elderly patients and veterans. 

According to United States Pennsylvania Attorney General; May 14, 2019: On May 02, 2019, a lawsuit was filed against Purdue Pharma, the creator of prescription painkiller OxyContin, accusing the company of a multi-faceted, illegal effort to market OxyContin in Pennsylvania. Shapiro’s suit is the first to specifically detail Purdue’s barrage of sales representatives targeting Pennsylvania doctors as a key facet of their campaign to push addictive opioids on Pennsylvanians.

The lawsuit alleges that Purdue launched an illegal marketing campaign of deception targeting Pennsylvania doctors and patients to change attitudes, practices, and the culture surrounding pain management. Some of the most egregious components of the campaign include Purdue deployed their highly trained sales staff to blanket Pennsylvania, making sales calls and in-person visits to physicians, totaling more than half a million visits in Pennsylvania alone, an amount second to only California. Purdue targeted Pennsylvania doctors with suspicious prescribing activity and would invest more sales force and marketing to get those doctors to prescribe even more OxyContin – sometimes resulting in as much as a 500% increase in OxyContin prescriptions by one office alone. Purdue misinformed doctors and pharmacists about the addictive nature of OxyContin and used industry thought leaders and in-house marketing literature to dispel the facts about the drug. As the opioid epidemic grew, Purdue created “pseudo-addiction,” a Purdue-conjured disease that showed similar equities as addiction but was to be treated, according to Purdue, with additional opioids. The Office of Attorney General is demanding that the Court issue an order preventing Purdue and anyone associated with Purdue’s misconduct from continuing to engage in these same deceptive tactics. 

According to United States Illinois Attorney General; April 08, 2019: On April 08, 2019, Lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma L.P. and Purdue Pharma Inc. over its deceptive marketing practices designed to significantly increase prescriptions issued for opioids.

According to Raoul, between 2008 and 2017, Purdue dispatched sales representatives to Illinois hundreds of thousands of times. Raoul alleged Purdue also funded third-party publications under the guise of educational materials to promote opioids and downplay their risks, using terms like “pseudo addiction.” Sales representatives informed doctors and patients that the risks could be controlled. Despite knowing that its opioid painkillers were dangerous and being misused and diverted, Purdue allegedly targeted doctors with addicted patients and whose patients were diverting drugs for unlawful use. Raoul alleged that Purdue’s tactics tripled prescriptions of its opioids in Illinois.

According to United States Oklahoma Attorney General and United States New York State Attorney General; March 28, 2019: The lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma LP for engaging in healthcare fraud. 

Pursuant to Executive Law § 63(12), From manufacturing, distributing, selling, or marketing opioids within the State unless it complies with heightened, independently-monitored safeguards against the recurrence of its fraudulent, illegal, and/or unlawful practices, which are to be set forth in a compliance plan reviewed and approved by Plaintiff and the Court.  Pursuant to Executive Law § 63(12), Pay restitution and damages for its fraudulent and/or illegal practices that violated that statute and caused compensable injuries to Plaintiff or any other person; and Disgorge all profits it wrongfully obtained as a result of its fraudulent and/or illegal practices in violation of that statute.

According to United States Tennessee Attorney General; March 26, 2019: On March 26, 2019, The settlement reached against purdue Pharma is a favorable development. After years of denial, Purdue finally recognized its role in creating the opioid crisis.At the same time, a recent Knox County circuit court ruling against Purdue will advance the litigation against the company for violating the state’s Consumer Protection Act. 

According to United States Utah Attorney General; January 30, 2019: The Utah Attorney General’s Office filed an administrative action against Purdue Pharma L.P. and others as part of the State’s efforts to hold accountable the opioid companies and individuals that created and fueled the opioid epidemic throughout Utah.

In the filing, under Utah Code, the Division of Consumer Protection of the Department of Commerce issued an administrative action, in the form of a citation, against the defendants alleging violations of the Utah Consumer Sales Practices Act. An administrative proceeding allows the State to seek to prove its claims and obtain a judgment, injunctive relief, and civil penalties more promptly than state district court proceedings. Based on evidence that has emerged over 2018, this administrative action alleges that not only Purdue, but two of its owners also participated in Purdue’s fraudulent conduct.

According to United States Connecticut Attorney General; December 20, 2018: The lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma L.P. and other affiliates for alleging that they designed, financed and waged a pervasive and aggressive campaign to mislead doctors and patients, claiming that prescription opioid medications manufactured and marketed by the company were safe and effective and strategically downplaying risks of addiction that they knew were inherent in their opioid products.

The state alleges that Purdue misinformed patients and doctors to get more and more people taking its premier opioid drug, OxyContin, and its two other opioid medications, Hysingla and Butrans. Purdue allegedly led patients and doctors to believe that opioids were safe to treat even minor pain, and that patients could and should take higher and more dangerous doses. The state alleges that Purdue sent sales representatives to doctors' offices, clinics, pharmacies and hospitals in Connecticut to make deceptive sales pitches about opioid drugs; rewarded high-prescribing doctors with attention, meals, gifts and money; and awarded prizes and bonuses to sales representatives who generated the most opioid prescriptions. In Connecticut, 1038 people died of accidental drug overdoses in 2017, the vast majority from opioid-related overdoses. The Connecticut Office of the Chief Medical Examiner has projected that 1030 more people will die of overdoses in 2018. From 2013 to 2016, Connecticut experienced a fourfold increase in deaths from prescription opioid overdoses, and the estimated economic cost of the opioid epidemic in Connecticut in 2016 was USD 10,270,000,000.

According to US-Florida Attorney General: November 16, 2018: An amended complaint was filed against opioid manufacturers and distributors including Purdue Pharma L.P.

Allegedly, defendants deceptively, unfairly, and unconscionably sought to convince prescribers and patients that opioids are safe, rarely addictive, and necessary for treating a wide range of common ailments. Defendants spread these myths knowing that opioids create physical dependency within days or weeks; that withdrawal from prescription opioids can be agonizing; that long-term and high-dose opioid use is particularly likely to lead to addiction; and that high doses of opioids can be fatal. Defendants at all levels of the supply chain manufacturers, distributors, and chain pharmacies continued selling opioids in Florida even though they knew or should have known that the drugs were being diverted and misused for non-medical purposes. Defendants had duties to identify and stop suspicious orders and purchases, and to put in place reasonable policies to safeguard against diversion.

According to the US-Oregon Department of Justice Office of the Attorney General; September 13, 2018: The complaint alleges that Purdue deceptively marketed OxyContin to Oregon seniors, misrepresented the risks and benefits of the drug, and lied to the Oregon Board of Pharmacy, all to maximize Purdue’s profits. It states that over the last decade Purdue has engaged in a pattern of racketeering and misleading activity in Oregon.

he complaint, filed in Multnomah Circuit Court, details how Purdue’s conduct violated an agreed upon stipulated 2007 Oregon judgment resulting from an earlier investigation of its unlawful practices, as well as four distinct Oregon laws: The Unlawful Trade Practices Act, the Elderly Persons and Persons with Disabilities Abuse Prevention Act, the False Claims Act and the Oregon Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act.

According to the U.S. Rhode Island Attorney General and US-Virginia Attorney General ; June, 2018: On June 25, 2018,  A civil lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma L.P., for prescription opioid manufacturers and distributors over their alleged campaign of unfairly, deceptively, and fraudulently marketing and promoting opioids in Rhode Island.

According to the Complaint, distributors persistently disregarded their obligations to identify suspicious orders and customers, facilitating and failing to stop the diversion of opioids within and to Rhode Island. Rhode Island's Medicaid program spent more than USD 6,000,000 to pay for prescriptions of Purdue-branded opioids, along with additional funds for Purdue's generic opioids and for the costs of providing and using opioids long-term to treat chronic pain.

According to the U.S. Florida Attorney General, U.S. North Dakota Attorney General and U.S. Texas Attorney General; May 15, 2018: A lawsuit was filed against Purdue Pharma L.P. for allegedly using a campaign of misrepresentations and omissions about the use of opioids to doctors and consumers in order to increase prescriptions and opioid use, including false statements about the addictive nature of opioids and omissions of the severe risks posed by taking opioids. 

The opioid distributors allegedly shipped inordinately high volumes of opioids to customers in Florida and failed to report these suspicious orders of opioids, thereby fueling widespread diversion of opioids throughout the state. In the complaint filed the defendants’ actions violated the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, the Florida RICO Act, and violated common law public nuisance and negligence. 

According to the US-Delaware Attorney General and the Department of Justice; January 19, 2018: On January 19, 2018 A lawsuit filed against Purdue Pharma LP  for engaging in false, deceptive and unfair marketing of prescription opioids.

Purdue Pharma LP engaged, and continue to engage, in a massive marketing campaign to misstate and conceal the risks of treating chronic pain with opioids. Although manufacturers are prohibited from marketing opioids through misstatements or omissions of material facts, Manufacturer Defendants nonetheless disseminated misstatements through multiple channels. This campaign includes websites, promotional materials, conferences, guidelines for doctors, and other vehicles. 

Purdue Pharma L.P. (together with Purdue Pharma Inc. and The Purdue Frederick Company, “Purdue”) is a limited partnership organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware with its principal place of business located in Stamford, Connecticut. Purdue Pharma L.P. has engaged in consensual commercial dealings with Delaware and its citizens, and has purposefully availed itself of the advantages of conducting business with and within Delaware.

row.profile_notes:
According to US-Illinois Attorney General; August 13, 2020: On August 13, 2020, Kirtikumar Patel and Prakashkumar Patel were charged with theft of government funds over USD 100,000, a Class X felony, and sales tax evasion over USD 100,000, a Class 1 felony. Prakashkumar Patel was also charged with two counts of filing a fraudulent Illinois income tax return, Class 4 felonies. Prakashkumar Patel is the owner of Blue Star 2, a convenience store, which Kirtikumar Patel managed. 

Between March 2013 and March 2018, the store collected the correct sales tax on purchases, but both men underreported sales tax numbers to the store’s accountant. The men reported a higher number of low-tax-rate sales than the store actually made, and underreported high-tax-rate sales and total receipts. The store’s accountant filed monthly sales tax returns, which were fraudulent since they were based on the underreported income. In the meantime, Prakashkumar and Kirtikumar kept the excess sales tax money.

On May 15, 2025, the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs imposed sanctions against Omar Ali Hussain.

On June 04, 2021, the Minister of State of Monaco imposed sanctions against Omar Ali HUSSAIN.

On December 31, 2020, the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office designated OMAR ALI HUSSAIN.

On November 24, 2016, the Trinidad and Tobago Financial Intelligence Unit listed OMAR on its Targeted Financial Sanctions List.

On March 17, 2016, OMAR ALI HUSSAIN was added to the Indonesian Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Center Suspected Terrorists and Terrorist Organizations list.

On September 29, 2015, the United States Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control designated Omar HUSSAIN under the Specially Designated Nationals List.

On September 28, 2015, the Council of the European Union imposed sanctions on Omar Ali Hussain regarding Regulation 2015/1815 imposing certain specific restrictive measures directed against certain persons and entities associated with the Al-Qaida network.

On September 18, 2015, the United Nations Security Council imposed sanctions against Omar Ali Hussain for being a foreign fighter for the Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant. UK national Hussain was considered to be one of ISIL’s most prominent recruiters. As an ISIL fighter, he offered tips on evading British security to individuals interested in leaving the United Kingdom to fight with ISIL.

According to Financial Supervisory Authority of Norway; February 27, 2023: On February 08, 2023, the Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa issued a warning against Binanfx. Binanfx was not authorized to offer investment services in Italy.

According to Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores de España; February 22, 2023: On February 13, 2023, the Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa issued a warning against Binanfx. Binanfx was not authorized to offer investment services in Italy.

According to International Organization of Securities Commissions; February 17, 2023: On February 17, 2023, the International Organization of Securities Commissions placed N 26 Pty Ltd on a list of unauthorized entities following an order issued by the Italian Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa.

According to Italy Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa; February 13, 2023: On February 08, 2023, the Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa ordered the black-out of Binanfx and its websites, www.binanfx.com and https://account.binanfx.com, for offering financial services illegally.

According to Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores de España; February 01, 2023: On January 19, 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority of the United Kingdom issued a warning against Binanfx. Binanfx was not authorized to offer investment services in the United Kingdom.

According to Italy Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa; January 23, 2023: On January 23, 2023, the Commissione Nazionale per le Società e la Borsa placed Binakfx on a list of unauthorized entities following a warning from Financial Conduct Authority of United Kingdom. According to the source, the company and its website offered financial services without the required authorization.

According to Financial Supervision Authority of Estonia and the Slovene Securities Market Agency; January 20, 2023: On January 20, 2023, the Financial Supervision Authority of Estonia placed Binanfx on an unauthorized companies list following a warning issued by the Financial Conduct Authority of the United Kingdom.

According to United Kingdom Financial Conduct Authority, the International Organization of Securities Commissions, the Financial Supervisory of Norway, the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority, the Netherlands Authority for the Financial Markets, the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority and the Financial Supervisory Authority of Finland; January 19, 2023: On January 19, 2023, Binanfx has been providing financial services or products in the United Kingdom without appropriate authorization by FCA.

row.profile_notes:
According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; December 15, 2025: N26 Bank SE must take appropriate and effective measures to establish a proper business organization. This was ordered by the financial regulator BaFin. BaFin has also appointed a special representative who will monitor compliance with the measures and report to BaFin on the progress of implementation. In addition, BaFin has set additional capital requirements and business restrictions for the institution. The bank is no longer allowed to conduct new business with mortgage loans in the Netherlands. The institute is also prohibited from securitizing claims from this transaction.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 21, 2024: The Federal Financial Supervisory Authority BaFin has imposed a fine of EUR 9 200 000 on N26 Bank AG for systematically late submission of suspicious transaction report in 2022. The fine notice is legally binding.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; July 17, 2023: On March 31, 2023, the Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) extended anti-money laundering measures against N26 Bank AG in addition to its order made on May 11, 2021, and specified them. The growth restrictions for new customers and the mandate of the special representative remain in place. Despite some progress, the institution still has deficiencies in its systems for preventing money laundering and terrorist financing. The decision made on March 31, 2023 is final.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; November 09, 2021: On October 05, 2021, the BaFin ordered N26 Bank GmbH to take measures to ensure a proper business organization and to mitigate risks to the institution's operational resilience. In accordance with section 45b (1) sentence 1 of the German Banking Act, BaFin has ordered risk mitigation measures that place limits on customer growth and on certain risk exposures. Customer acquisition is to be substantially reduced with N26 Bank GmbH only permitted to acquire a maximum of 50 000 new customers per month. In addition, the value of exposures secured by mortgages on immovable property may not exceed EUR 500 000 000. This limitation is applicable in all countries in which N26 Bank GmbH operates. A special commissioner appointed by BaFin will monitor implementation of the measures ordered. The order has been final and binding since November 06, 2021. This order should also be considered in relation to the order issued by BaFin on May 11, 2021 to rectify deficiencies related to the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; September 29, 2021: On June 25, 2021, BaFin imposed a fine in the amount of EUR 4 250 000 against N26 Bank GmbH on the basis of section 56 para. 1 no. 69 of the Act on the Detection of Proceeds from Serious Crimes (Money Laundering Act). The decision came into force on July 15, 2021.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 12, 2021: On May 11, 2021, the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) ordered N26 Bank GmbH to implement appropriate internal controls and safeguards and comply with general due diligence requirements, in order to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing. The BaFin also ordered the bank to rectify deficiencies both in IT monitoring and in customer due diligence. In order to monitor the implementation of the measures, the BaFin is appointing a special commissioner. The notice has been final and binding since May 11, 2021.

According to the Germany Bafin Federal Financial Supervisory Authority; May 22, 2019: On May 20, 2019, the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) issued an order against N26 Bank GmbH to take appropriate internal safety measures and to comply with general Customer Due Diligence obligations. Moreover, N26 Bank GmbH has to ensure the existence of an adequate personnel and technical-organisational equipment in order to comply with its obligations under money laundering law. The decision became legal on May 20, 2019.

row.profile_notes:
According to United States Attorney - Southern District of New York and U.S. Internal Revenue Service; September 12, 2023: Karl Sebastian Greenwood was sentenced to 20 years in prison for his orchestration of the massive OneCoin fraud scheme. Greenwood was ordered to pay approximately USD 300 million in forfeiture.

According to United States Attorney - Southern District of New York and U.S. Internal Revenue Service; December 16, 2022: On December 16, 2022, Karl Sebastian Greenwood, who co-founded OneCoin, pled guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, one count of wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering in connection with his participation in the massive OneCoin fraud scheme.  OneCoin, which began operations in 2014 and was based in Sofia, Bulgaria, marketed and sold a fraudulent cryptocurrency by the same name through a global multi-level-marketing (MLM) network.  As a result of misrepresentations that Greenwood and others made about OneCoin, victims invested over four billion dollars worldwide in the fraudulent cryptocurrency. 

Greenwood and his co-conspirators, including fugitive Ruja Ignatova, conned unsuspecting victims out of billions of dollars, claiming that OneCoin would be the Bitcoin killer.  In fact, OneCoins were entirely worthless. OneCoin operated as a MLM network through which members received commissions for recruiting others to purchase cryptocurrency packages.  Greenwood and other OneCoin leaders also claimed that the OneCoin cryptocurrency was “mined” using mining servers maintained and operated by the company.  In fact, OneCoins were never mined using computer resources. Greenwood was arrested at his residence on the island of Koh Samui, Thailand, in July 2018, and was extradited to the United States to face fraud and money laundering charges in October 2018. Greenwood has been detained since his arrest in July 2018.

According to U.S. Federal Bureau of Prisons; as of December 01, 2021:

According to news.bitcoin.com and justicenewsflash.com; November 25, 2021: Karl Sebastian Greenwood, sentenced to jail is accused of using smuggled mobile phones to transfer 20 million US dollars. Greenwood, currently detained at the Metropolitan Correctional Center. 

According to storage.courtlistener.com; April 21, 2021: Superseding Indictment filed against Karl Sebastian Greenwood for conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy.

According to thecoinrise.com; 2020: In March 2018, Sebastian Greenwood was indicted, arrested in Thailand in November 2018 and extradited to the United States. The US prosecutors charge Greenwood with five counts comprising conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money-laundering, conspiracy to commit securities fraud, and securities fraud. The indictment accuses Greenwood of being responsible for the scamming and money laundering of USD 1,000,000,000 of OneCoin. The sale of OneCoin packages is also considered securities fraud. The US prosecutors do not consider OneCoin to be a cryptocurrency.

According to comsuregroup.com; April 17, 2020: On February 06, 2018, indictment filed and unsealed in April, 2020, alleges that Karl Sebastian Greenwood personally conspired with several others to embezzle at least USD 1,000,000,000 through fraudulent sales of the cryptocurrency OneCoin. As alleged, defendants created a multi-billion dollar cryptocurrency company based completely on lies and deceit. They promised big returns and minimal risk, but, as alleged, this business was a pyramid scheme based on smoke and mirrors more than zeroes and ones.

According to storage.courtlistener.com; April 06, 2020: Indictment filed against Karl Sebastian Greenwood for conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, conspiracy to commit securities fraud and securities Fraud.

Abdul Rahman Yasin was born on 10 April 1960.

On December 31, 2020, the United Kingdom under the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office added ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN under its sanctions list. 

On November 24, 2016, the Trinidad and Tobago Financial Intelligence Unit listed ABDUL RAHMAN on its Targeted Financial Sanctions List.

On March 17, 2016, ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN was added to the Indonesian Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Center Suspected Terrorists and Terrorist Organizations list.

On October 17, 2001, the United Nations Security Council imposed sanctions on ABDUL RAHMAN YASIN for being associated with Al-Qaida. Yasin directly assisted terrorist mastermind Ramzi Ahmed Yousef in carrying out the February 26, 1993, World Trade Center bombing in New York City. Yasin fled the United States immediately after the bombing to avoid arrest. He was indicted in the United States for his role in the World Trade Center bombing. He is wanted for his alleged participation in the terrorist bombing of the World Trade Center, New York City, on February 26, 1993, which resulted in six deaths, the wounding of numerous individuals, and the significant destruction of property and commerce.

The Rewards For Justice Program, United States Department of State, is offering a reward of up to USD 25,000,000 for information leading directly to the apprehension or conviction of Abdul Rahman Yasin.

Abdul Yasin was born in 1960 in Bloomington, Ind., where his Iraqi father was a graduate student, and grew up in Baghdad. He returned to the United States in the early 1990's, to live with his mother and a brother who were living in Jersey City. It was then that he met Ramzi Yousef. Yousef recruited Yasin for the plot to blow up the World Trade Center. Mr. Yasin helped mix the chemicals used in the blast, at one point severely burning his leg. 

Abdul Yasin lived with several of the WTC conspirators at 34 Kensington Ave in Jersey City. The FBI initially detained Mr. Yasin after the attack and then released him. After it realized its error, the FBI placed Abdul Yasin on the list of "Most Wanted" terrorists, but it was too late. On the evening of March 5th, Yasin departed the United States on a Royal Jordanian Airlines flight. The FBI believes that Yasin flew to Jordan and then drove twelve hours to Baghdad, where he has relatives. 

A reporter for ABC News spotted Yasin in Baghdad in 1994 and reported that he was operating freely. A neighbor told the reporter that Yasin was working for the Iraqi government. Documents recovered from postwar Iraq indicate that Yasin received no only safe haven in Iraq, but also funding from the former Iraqi regime. In an interview with the CBS News program "60 Minutes" in June 2002, Mr. Yasin admitted his involvement in the World Trade Center bombing and expressed regret for what he had done. "I'm very sorry for what happened," he said. "I don't know what to do to make it up." Abdul Rahman Yasin is still at large. The United States Department of State is offering a reward of up to $5 million for information leading directly to his apprehension or conviction. 

Yasin is believed to still be in Iraq.

row.profile_notes:
According to elpais.com; October 28, 2021: Luis Bárcenas was sentenced to two years in prison for forgery, fraud and tax evasion. The National Court issued a ruling in relation to the reform of the headquarters of the Popular Party (PP) after having considered proven that Bárcenas paid the Unifica company more than EUR 1,000,000 outside of the official billing and accounting, funds that were not declared to the Public Treasury. According to the Hearing, Bárcenas managed the cash funds that were contributed to the PP as private donations through a parallel accounting, of which the income and expenses were not recorded in the official accounting and, therefore, were not audited by the Court of Accounts. Consequently, a fine of EUR 1,200,000 was imposed on Bárcenas for having been a necessary cooperator of a crime of accounting falsification in relation to another against the Treasury for the fraud to the treasury of the Unifica Corporation Tax of 2007.

According to elconfidencial.com; February 22, 2021: The National High Court agreed to commence the repatriation of EUR 50,342,107 that different convicted persons in the Gürtel case, among whom was Luis Bárcenas, had in Switzerland. The objective was to have at the disposal of the court the amounts that had been blocked in various banks in the aforementioned country, which included Credit Suisse, Lombard Odier, LGT Bank, Banque SYZ and Mirabaud. According to the decree, around EUR 22,400,000 were in accounts owned by Bárcenas.

According to antena3.com; February 08, 2021: On February 08, 2021, Luis Bárcenas was facing trial for corruption, forgery and tax evasion. The case was related to the alleged box B of the Popular Party (PP), which is why Bárcenas was going to have to answer for the irregular payment of the reform of the headquarters of the PP on Genova street and for the purchase of shares of a half with money from box B. Likewise, Bárcenas exposed as responsible for an irregular financing institutionalized since 1982, the old leadership headed by Mariano Rajoy.

According to elmundo.es; October 14, 2020: The Supreme Court notified the sentence of the piece Epoca I of the Gürtel plot (1999 - 2005), confirming the sentences imposed by the National High Court on the main leaders of the corruption network as well as that of the Popular Party. The Chamber upheld the sentence of the leader of the plot; however, it reduced the sentences for several of those involved, among them, Luis Bárcenas, who was reduced to 29 years and one month in prison. The Supreme Court took into consideration the appeal of Bárcenas, resulting in the reduction of the sentence for money laundering, exclusion of the crime of forgery and the acquittal of the crime of procedural fraud.

According to nuevodiariodesalta.com.ar; June 02, 2018: Luis Barcenas was part of the case where the La Moraleja Company was involved in a plot of crimes of corruption and money laundering, in which Ángel Sanchis, Ángel Sanchis Herrero were the main architects after diverting EUR 3,000,000 through the company mentioned. The ruling mentions Bárcenas as a fundamental piece, who granted the aforementioned amount to Sanchis Perales as a loan on behalf of the Sinequanon Foundation, however, the funds came out of the Bárcenas account in the name of the Panamanian foundation that the latter had in the Dresdner Bank of Switzerland towards another of the HSBC in New York in charge of Brixo SA, an entity in Uruguay linked to the Sanchís family. Subsequently, part of the funds were transferred to accounts of another Sanchis company, Argentina's La Moraleja SA, through which the aforementioned individuals devised a complex scheme to reimburse the money to Bárcenas. Consequently, all those involved received their respective convictions after it was verified that these knew the illicit origin of the funds.

According to vanitatis.elconfidencial.com; May 24, 2018: Luis Bárcenas was sentenced to 33 years in prison for money laundering, tax evasion, forgery and fraud. Luis Bárcenas and other associates were involved in the Gürtel case and used Grupo Correa and Partido Popular to issue inflated invoices or invoices that did not respond to real services and were paid out of municipal public funds.

According to lainformacion.com; October 02, 2016: The trial of the case Gürtel was schedule on October 04, 2016. The defendants were 37 people including Jose Luis Barcenas Gutierrez, who were accused of fraud, corruption, financial crimes, bribery, forgery and embezzlement for committing irregular activities developed between the years 1999 and 2005. The oral hearing would take place in the headquarters in San Fernando de Henares.

According to efe.com; April 27, 2015: The Prosecutor's Office requested 5 years in prison and fined EUR 265,000 against José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez for the "Bárcenas case". De acuerdo con elpais.com; Octubre 28, 2021: Luis Bárcenas fue sentenciado a dos años en prisión por falsedad documental, fraude y evasión de impuestos. La Audiencia Nacional dictó sentencia en relación a la reforma de la sede central del Partido Popular (PP) después de haber considerado probado que Bárcenas abono a la empresa Unifica más de un EUR 1,000,000 al margen de la facturación y contabilidad oficial, fondos que no fueron declarados a Hacienda Pública. Según la Audiencia, Bárcenas gestionó los fondos en efectivo que se aportaron al PP como donaciones privadas a través de una contabilidad paralela, de la cual, el ingreso y gasto no se dejó constancia en la contabilidad oficial y, por ende, no fueron fiscalizada por el Tribunal de Cuentas. Consecuentemente, se impuso para Bárcenas una multa de EUR 1,200,000 por haber sido cooperador necesario de un delito de falsedad contable en relación con otro contra Hacienda por el fraude al fisco del Impuesto de Sociedades de 2007 de Unifica.

De acuerdo con elconfidencial.com; Febrero 22, 2021: La Audiencia Nacional acordó poner en marcha la repatriación de EUR 50,342,107 que distintos condenados por el caso Gürtel, entre los que estaba Luis Bárcenas, tenían en Suiza. El objetivo era tener a disposición del tribunal las cantidades que habían permanecido bloqueadas en diversos bancos del mencionado país, en los que figuraban Credit Suisse, Lombard Odier, LGT Bank, Banque SYZ y Mirabaud. Según el decreto, alrededor de EUR 22,400,000 figuraban en cuentas de las que Bárcenas era titular.

De acuerdo con antena3.com; Febrero 08, 2021: En Febrero 08, 2021, Luis Bárcenas estaba enfrentando juicio por corrupción, falsedad documental y evasión fiscal. El caso estaba relacionado a la presunta caja B del Partido Popular (PP), motivo por el cual Bárcenas iba a tener que responder por el pago irregular de la reforma de la sede del PP en la calle Génova y por la compra de acciones de un medio con dinero de la caja B. Así mismo, Bárcenas exponía como responsables de una financiación irregular institucionalizada desde 1982, a la antigua cúpula encabezada por Mariano Rajoy.

De acuerdo con elmundo.es; Octubre 14, 2020: El Tribunal Supremo notificó la sentencia de la pieza Época I de la trama Gürtel (1999 – 2005), confirmando las condenas impuestas por la Audiencia Nacional a los principales líderes de la red de corrupción así como la del Partido Popular. La Sala mantuvo la condena del líder de la trama, sin embargo, redujo las condenas para varios de los implicados, entre ellos, Luis Bárcenas, a quien se redujo a 29 años y un mes en prisión. El Supremo tomó en consideración el recurso de Bárcenas, resultando en la reducción de la condena por blanqueo de capitales, exclusión del delito de falsedad documental y la absolución del delito de estafa procesal.

De acuerdo con nuevodiariodesalta.com.ar; Junio 02, 2018: Luis Bárcenas fue parte del caso donde la Empresa La Moraleja estuvo implicada en una trama de delitos de corrupción y lavado de dinero, en la cual Ángel Sanchis, Ángel Sanchis Herrero fueron los principales artífices tras desviar EUR 3,000,000 a través de la empresa mencionada. La sentencia menciona como pieza fundamental a Bárcenas, quien concedió la cantidad ya mencionada a Sanchis Perales en calidad de préstamo a nombre de la Fundación Sinequanon, sin embargo, los fondos salieron de la cuenta de Bárcenas a nombre de la fundación panameña que este último tenía en el Dresdner Bank de Suiza hacia otra del HSBC en Nueva York a cargo de Brixo SA, entidad en Uruguay vinculada a la familia Sanchís. Posteriormente, parte de los fondos fueron transferidos a cuentas de otra sociedad de los Sanchis, la argentina La Moraleja SA, a través de la cual, los individuos mencionados idearon una compleja trama para reintegrar el dinero a Bárcenas. Consecuentemente, todos los involucrados recibieron sus respectivas condenas después de comprobarse que estos conocían el origen ilícito de los fondos.

De acuerdo con vanitatis.elconfidencial.com; May 24, 2018: Luis Bárcenas fue sentenciado a 33 años en prisión por blanqueo de dinero, fraude fiscal, falsedad documental y estafa procesal. Luis Bárcenas y asociados estaban envueltos en la trama Gürtel y usaban al Grupo Correa y Partido Popular para emitir facturas infladas o que no respondían a servicios reales y se abonaban con cargo a los fondos públicos municipales.

De acuerdo con lainformacion.com; Octubre 02, 2016: El inicio del juicio del caso Gürtel fue programado en  Octubre 4, 2016. La audiencia oral se llevaría a cabo en la sede en San Fernando de Henares.

De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Marzo 06, 2015: El Juez de Audiencia Nacional ordenó el juicio de 40 personas por su presunta participación en un plan de sobornos en el seno del Partido Popular (PP). José Luis Bárcenas fue uno de los 40 individuos y jefe principal del caso.

De acuerdo con 20minutos.es; Enero 22, 2015: José Luis Bárcenas fue puesto en libertad bajo fianza por Pablo Ruz, juez de la Audiencia Nacional, después de pagar una fianza de EUR 200,000 impuesta por el Sr. Ruz. Además del dinero, Luis Bárcenas está obligado a presentarse ante la Corte Nacional todos los lunes, miércoles y viernes, dar su dirección y permanecer en España.

De acuerdo con elmundo.es; Febrero 26, 2014: Un informe de la Dirección Nacional de Investigación del Fraude (ONIF), reveló que el ex juez de la Audiencia Nacional ha rechazado por tercera vez una solicitud por Bárcenas Gutiérrez para ser puesto en libertad, después de la divulgación de dos cuentas bancarias en los Estados Unidos bajo su nombre. Tesorero del Partido Popular (PP) Bárcenas Gutiérrez defraudó a la Agencia Tributaria con un total de EUR 11,5 00,000 entre los años 2000 y 2011.

De acuerdo con elpais.com; Julio 23, 2013: El juez encargado del caso Gürtel, Pablo Ruz, solicitó a las autoridades uruguayas congelar todas las cuentas bancarias bajo el nombre de José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez o su compañía Tesedul, que fue supuestamente el frente para el lavado de dinero.

De acuerdo con publico.pt; Junio 27, 2013: El ex tesorero del Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas, fue arrestado por riesgo de fuga. Bárcenas fue acusado por el presunto envío de grandes sumas de dinero de las cuentas del partido político a Suiza y EE.UU. Fue enviado a prisión sin fianza, ya que había un riesgo grave de fuga o la posible manipulación y alteración de pruebas de una falsa compra y venta de obras de arte. Bárcenas fue a declarar el 27 de Junio, 2013, por la entrada de EUR 500,000 en su cuenta en las notas de EUR 500, durante el año 2006. Bárcenas reclamó el dinero de las ventas de obras de arte. Él está siendo investigado por blanqueo de capitales, crímenes contra la hacienda pública, fraude y falsedad en documento mercantil.

De acuerdo con elpais.com; Junio 13, 2013: De acuerdo con el informe de la Agencia Tributaria española, José Luis Bárcenas y su esposa, Rosalía Iglesias, defraudaron al Servicio de Impuestos Internos española con EUR 1,500,000 en 2002 y 2003. La pareja también tiene declaraciones de impuestos de EUR 21,795 euros durante esos años.

De acuerdo con 20minutos.es; Enero 16, 2013: De acuerdo con los informes de que el juez Pablo Ruz envió a las autoridades, el ex senador José Luis Bárcenas tenía EUR 22,000,000 en cuentas de bancos suizos, que fueron transferidos a otra cuenta, cuando fue acusado de corrupción por su participación en el caso Gürtel.

De acuerdo con rtve.es; Febrero 09, 2009: Luis Bárcenas fue imputado provisionalmente por corrupción, cohecho y fraude fiscal dentro de la Operación Gürtel. El caso Gürtel investigaba una presunta trama de corrupción y tráfico de influencias dirigida por el empresario Francisco Correa que se nutría de fondos de entidades públicas de las comunidades autónomas de Madrid y Valencia para "obtener un beneficio propio" y en la que estarían implicados varios cargos del Partido Popular. Luis Bárcenas estaba acusado de recibir EUR 1,300,000 de las empresas vinculadas con Correa a cambio de recibir concesiones de actos públicos del partido.

row.position_or_allegation: Permanently enjoined from securities related business for violating Securities Exchange Act - July 7, 2006
row.details: enforcement: Wire Fraud/Debarred/Securities Fraud | US-U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission | United States
row.relationships: Deep Rock Oil Company (AffiliatedCompany; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; July 10, 2006: On July 7, 2006, the Securities and Exchange Commission filed a settled civil action in Oklahoma City federal court against David W. Taylor, and his company, Deep Rock Oil Company. As part of the settlement, Taylor and Deep Rock, without admitting or denying the Commission's allegations consented to a final judgment enjoining them from violating the antifraud and registration provisions of the federal securities laws.

The Commission charges that Deep Rock and Taylor conducted a fraudulent unregistered offering of interests in two affiliated joint ventures that were to engage in natural gas exploration and production in the Greasy Creek field in Oklahoma. The SEC's complaint details that, from mid-2002 to mid-2004, Taylor and Deep Rock employed a variety of misrepresentations and omissions to raise approximately $2.5 million from nearly 100 investors. Among other things, the complaint alleges that Deep Rock and Taylor exaggerated or fabricated Taylor's industry experience and prior success in drilling profitable natural gas wells; downplayed or concealed the substantial risks associated with the investment; and grossly overstated the success of the joint ventures' operations. According to the Commission, Taylor also failed to inform investors of his prior conviction for wire fraud and securities violations for offering fraudulent oil and gas investments during the 1950s. 

The SEC's complaint alleges that Deep Rock and Taylor violated Sections 5(a), 5(c), and 17(a) of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 there under. Deep Rock and Taylor have consented to the entry of a final judgment permanently enjoining them from violating these provisions.

row.name: Jérôme Kerviel
row.position_or_allegation: Fined EUR 1,000,000 for bank fraud, forgery and securities fraud - September 23, 2016.
row.details: adverse_media: Bank Fraud/Securities Fraud/Forgery | Incident
row.relationships: Société Générale S.A. (AffiliatedCompany; AdverseMedia,Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to the leparisien.fr; September 23, 2016: On September 23, 2016, The Court of Appeal of Versailles ordered Jérôme Kerviel to pay EUR 1,000,000 in damages to the Société générale bank for forgery, breach of trust and fraud. Initially, the bank demanded Jerome Kerviel to pay EUR 4,900,000,000 allegedly lost in 2008 due to the fraudulent broker activities of Jerome Kerviel.

According to the lefigaro.fr; September 04, 2014: On September 04, 2014, the Appeal Court of Paris accepted the liberation of Jerome Kerviel if he wears an electronic bracelet.

According to the lepoint.fr; May 19, 2014: On May 19, 2014, Jerome Kerviel was imprisoned in Nice after being arrested at midnight in Menton just as he crossed the French Italian border. At exactly midnight Kerviel was meant to present himself to the authorities so he could begin serving a three-year prison sentence for forgery and embezzlement. Kerviel has spent the last two and a half months walking in Italy. 

According to the bbc.com; March 19, 2014: On March 19, 2014, Jerome Kerviel has lost his appeal against a three-year jail sentence. France's highest court upheld the jail sentence against Jerome Kerviel but ordered a review of the EUR 4,900,000,000 in damages he was told to pay.

According to the lemonde.fr; October 25, 2012: On October 24, 2012, the Court of Appeal of Paris confirmed the first instance sentence imposed on Jérôme Kerviel (five years imprisonment three of which are unconditional, and payment of compensation in the amount of about EUR 4,900,000,000). 

According to the bbc.co.uk; October 05, 2010: On October 05, 2010, Jérôme Kerviel, former Societe Generale trader, was sentenced to five years imprisonment, with two years suspended, by a court of Paris. He was found guilty of forgery, unauthorised computer uses and breach of trust. Kerviel was told to repay the damages in amount of 4,900,000,000 which were lost by the bank through his activity.

According to the reuters.com; January 26, 2008: On January 26, 2008, Jérôme Kerviel was brought into police custody in Paris, suspected of causing a USD 7,000,000,000 loss through rogue trades at Societe Generale, France's second-biggest listed bank.

row.name: Abdul Rahman
row.position_or_allegation: Arrested for fraud - December 2023.
row.details: adverse_media: Fraud/Forgery/Organized Crime | Incident
row.relationships: Dash, Rajesh (Associate; AdverseMedia); Tripathy, Biju (Associate; AdverseMedia); Dash, Prasanjit (Associate; AdverseMedia); Mantri, Mukesh (Associate; AdverseMedia); Samantara, Pradeep Kumar (Associate; AdverseMedia)
row.profile_notes: According to the odishabytes.com; December 23, 2023: In December 2023, Abdul Rahman was arrested along with other associates in connection with a credit card fraud amounting to INR 80,000,000. The complainant alleged that a credit card was issued in his name without his knowledge, and he was denied loan over poor CIBIL score because of the transactions made using it. The outstanding dues of the credit card was INR 140,000. During investigation identified Biju Tripathy as the person using the credit card. During the raid on his house, 450 credit and debit cards, INR 700,000 cash, 50 cheque books, 78 passbooks, 3 sacks of money receipt, six swipe machines and as many mobile phones were seized. Prasanjit Dash used to collect personal credentials of different persons to apply for credit cards and also fraudulently received those cards and used it. Simultaneously Pradeep Kumar Samantara, who was the employee of a bank, used to issue those cards in the name of Rakesh Kumar with forged documents. Mukesh Mantri introduced Prasanjit Dash with Biju Tripathy, who used to collect cash by using the credit card at POS counters like hospitals and OMFED booths in connivance with billing agents. Abdul Rahman and Rajesh Dash are hospital employees who worked as billing agents. Biju Tripathy used pay some commission to the billing agents and invest the remaining cash to earn profits. Police have calculated INR 20,000,000 of the money receipt seized.

row.details: enforcement: Terrorism | PK-Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) - Govt. of Pakistan | Pakistan
row.profile_notes:
According to the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) - Govt. of Pakistan; June 2014: Anti Terrorism Act 1997 inspite of various shortcomings has provided effective mechanism to police stations to conduct surveillance of activists on Schedule-IV of the Act in order to curb and prevent acts of terrorism by members of proscribed organizations. Section-11EE prescribes restrictions on movements, residence & visits of these suspects. Section 11EE also states that suspects before leaving the area of residence have to seek prior permission of Officer Incharge of Police Station. Their assets & sources of incomes will also be subject to investigation. ATA-1997 further provides that any person who violates any direction or order shall be punishable with an imprisonment of up to 3 years or fine or both. However, these provisions of ATA 1997 are not enforced effectively or uniformly. It is very rare to observe registration of cases against suspects u/s 11EE ATA 1997. CTW FIA has prepared the consolidated list of Activists on basis of data provided by CTD/CIDs and Home Departments.

Once all provinces have updated lists of Activists on Schedule-IV the Federal & Provincial Govts. may also consider some amendments in ATA in order to deny or restrict issuance of passports, arms licence, driving licence, credit card, internet usage etc to these suspects so that they cannot easily travel, associate, rent building, buy weapons/transport/ dual use chemicals, harborterrorists, use internet etc, and conduct terrorist attacks freely.

One of the suspects listed by District Quetta is: Abdul Rahman

Father's Name: Abdul Aziz cast Syed 
Address/Police Station: Kuchlak Bazar Quetta
Position: Terrorist
Party Affiliation: Terrorist
Remarks: Personal file not yet be opened by local Police, no monitoring reported.

row.profile_notes:
According to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; January 10, 2017: On January 10, 2017, The Securities and Exchange Commission announced that the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey has agreed to admit wrongdoing and pay a USD 400,000 penalty to settle charges that it was aware of risks to a series of New Jersey roadway projects but failed to inform investors purchasing the bonds that would fund them.

The SEC’s order finds that the Port Authority offered and sold USD 2,300,000,000 worth of bonds to investors despite internal discussions about whether certain projects outlined in offering documents, including the Pulaski Skyway, ventured outside its mandate and potentially weren’t legal to pursue.  One internal memo noted, “There is no clear path to legislative authority to undertake such projects.” Another memo explicitly identified “the risk of a successful challenge by the bondholders and investors” in connection with the funding of the roadway projects.  But the Port Authority omitted any mention in its offering documents about these risks surrounding its ability to fund the projects.  Its offering documents stated that it issued bonds “only for purposes for which the Port Authority is authorized by law to issue bonds.”

The Port Authority is the first municipal issuer to admit wrongdoing in an SEC enforcement action. The SEC’s order finds that the Port Authority violated Sections 17(a)(2) and 17(a)(3) of the Securities Act of 1933. The SEC’s order acknowledges the Port Authority’s cooperation and prompt remedial acts. The projects at issue have proceeded as planned.

According to money.cnn.com, nbcnewyork.com and philly.com; September 25, 2015: U.S. Department of Justice opens probe into Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. The Port Authority has adopted new ethics rules as federal prosecutors probe potential wrongdoing at the agency, involving billions of dollars in public works projects.

The U.S. attorney's office in New Jersey has been investigating the Port Authority and particularly former chairman David Samson, who stepped down in early 2014. Prosecutors have subpoenaed numerous documents from the agency pertaining to contracts that include two bridge projects and a highway project in New Jersey, as well as the Port Authority's conflict of interest and recusal policies. When Samson was in charge at the Port Authority, United Airlines resumed direct flights to the South Carolina airport near his vacation home. Around the same time, United was pressing for concessions from the agency, including a new hangar at the Newark airport, rent reductions and a commuter rail-line extension that would connect the airport directly to lower Manhattan.

row.relationships: Ansarullah Bangla Team (AffiliatedOrganization; Enforcement,Sanction)
row.profile_notes:
According to the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) - Govt. of Pakistan; June 2014: Anti Terrorism Act 1997 inspite of various shortcomings has provided effective mechanism to police stations to conduct surveillance of activists on Schedule-IV of the Act in order to curb and prevent acts of terrorism by members of proscribed organizations. Section-11EE prescribes restrictions on movements, residence & visits of these suspects. Section 11EE also states that suspects before leaving the area of residence have to seek prior permission of Officer In charge of Police Station. Their assets & sources of incomes will also be subject to investigation. ATA-1997 further provides that any person who violates any direction or order shall be punishable with an imprisonment of up to 3 years or fine or both. However, these provisions of ATA 1997 are not enforced effectively or uniformly. It is very rare to observe registration of cases against suspects u/s 11EE ATA 1997. CTW FIA has prepared the consolidated list of Activists on basis of data provided by CTD/CIDs and Home Departments.

Once all provinces have updated lists of Activists on Schedule-IV the Federal & Provincial Govts. may also consider some amendments in ATA in order to deny or restrict issuance of passports, arms licence, driving licence, credit card, internet usage etc to these suspects so that they cannot easily travel, associate, rent building, buy weapons/transport/ dual use chemicals, harbor terrorists, use internet etc, and conduct terrorist attacks freely.

According to ilgiorno.it; September 23, 2015: In September 2015, Giampiero Fiorani was sent on trial by the Prosecutors of Lodi, for subtraction fraudulent payment of taxes. According to the authorities, he transferred the two houses that he owned to his relatives without paying taxes.

According to ilgiorno.it; November 09, 2012: In November 2012 Giampiero Fiorani, former Head of Banca Popolare di Lodi, was sentenced by the Court of Appeal of Nice, to one year of imprisonment and a fine of EUR 300.000 euros for money laundering. The facts dates back in 2003, when the former banker bought for 3 million euro a seaside villa in Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, one of the most exclusive French Riviera. The operation was carried out through the company Liberty, owned in equal parts by two acquaintances of Fiorani. In 2006, Fiorani acquired 45% of the company from one of the two owners and few months later, he sold it to a real estate agent in Monaco.

According to ilfattoquotidiano.it; May 28, 2012: On May 28, 2011 Giampiero Fiorani, was sentenced, to one year and eight months of imprisonment for inside trading and embezzlement in the process called “Antonveneta”. One year later, on May 28, 2012 the sentence was reduced on appeal to one year.

row.profile_notes:
According to the roscommonherald.ie; August 10, 2022: On August 10, 2022, Farah Damji was arrested on by gardaí at a property in rural Co Galway before being brought before the vacation sitting of the High Court in Dublin. The High Court has remanded Damji in custody, who is wanted in the UK to serve out the remainder of her prison sentence for stalking and breaching a restraining order. She has several fraud convictions in a number of jurisdictions, was arrested on foot of a bench warrant issued over her alleged failure to appear before courts that were considering the extradition request.

According to the independent.ie; June 28, 2022: In June 2022, A bench warrant has been issued for the arrest of notorious international conwoman Farah Damji, who lost a Supreme Court bid to prevent her extradition to the UK and has failed to appear before a scheduled sitting of the High Court.

According to the roscommonherald.ie; June 16, 2022: In June 2022, Supreme court upholds decision to extradite on-the-run fraudster Farah Damji to the UK. She will be extradited to the United Kingdom to serve the remainder of her sentence for stalking-type offences and breaching a restraining order after the Supreme Court dismissed her appeal.

According to the irishtimes.com; January 31, 2022: The High Court has ordered the extradition of on-the-run fraudster Farah Damji to the UK, where she is wanted for fleeing a trial. She has been remanded on continuing bail, as the court heard she intends to appeal the decision.

According to the irishtimes.com; August 17, 2020: On August 17, 2020, Farah Damji also known as Farah Dan, was arrested in Dublin. A search was carried out at a block of apartments in Dublin’s north inner city, close to Bachelor’s Walk, where she was located and arrested. She had fled to Ireland while on the run amid a trial in London in which she was convicted and sentenced in her absence. She was convicted in February on two counts of breaching a restraining order, in April 2018 and June 2018. Following her conviction in her absence, she was sentenced in March to 27 months in jail and a European Arrest Warrant was issued for her. She has a long and storied criminal career stretching back to the early 1990s, when she ran an art gallery in New York and East Hampton.

According to the dailymail.co.uk; January 29, 2010: On January 29, 2010, Farah Damji, daughter of multi-millionaire property tycoon Amir Damji, was sentenced to 15 months in prison for a GBP 17,500 housing benefit fraud. She admitted three counts of dishonestly making false representations to Hammersmith and Fulham Council, a letting agency and a landlord. She had already served for three-and-a-half years after being found guilty at Blackfriars Crown Court in October 2005 for stealing a credit card and fraudulently spending GBP 50,000.

row.profile_notes:
According to lavozdegalicia.es; October 06, 2020: The National Court fined Pescanova with EUR 30 per day for two years for fraud and forgery. In addition, 11 individuals also involved in the case were sentenced for accounting fraud that was designed to obtain bank financing for Pescanova, as well as the manipulation of accounts in order to attract investors. Due to the acts carried out by those involved in the case, in 2013 there were losses of almost EUR 800,000,000 and EUR 3,600,000, which led to the bankruptcy of Pescanova.

According to elcorreogallego.es; June 04, 2020: The Civil Chamber of the Supreme Court rejected the appeal presented by Nueva Pescanova to the sentence passed in December 2016, in which the request that the old company faced the payment of different amounts was rejected, an agreement that had place in 2015 between the two companies. The ruling dismissed the claim of EUR 1,090,000 withheld by Pescanova plus interest accrued since 2015 as well as another EUR 800,000 for administrative expenses.

According to lavozdegalicia.es; January 28, 2020: Pescanova SA, the old company, was going to go to trial in the National Court along with all the former senior officials of the multinational. The 19 people and the 11 legal entities were accused of having altered the financial statements between 2009 and 2012, to hide the company's millionaire losses. Pescanova SA, stated that Nueva Pescanova, which arose after the bankruptcy, was going to be in charge of the economic consequences of the hypothetical condemnatory sentence. Additionally, the judge imposed a fine of EUR 262,000,000 and EUR 348,200,000 of bail for Pescanova SA.

According to europapress.es; November 28, 2015: The National Securities Market Commission (CNMV) imposed two fines on Pescanova for a total amount of EUR 450,000 and two others to the former executive president of the company Manuel Fernández de Sousa-Faro for EUR 225,000 for infractions of the Securities Market Law , according to the Official State Gazette (BOE), both the Galician company and its then president have been fined for carrying out market manipulation practices between January 29 and April 29, 2009.


De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Octubre 06, 2020: La Audiencia Nacional multó a Pescanova con EUR 30 por día durante dos años por fraude y falsedad de documentos. Además 11 individuos también involucrados en la causa fueron sentenciados por el fraude contable que fue diseñado para obtener financiación bancaria para Pescanova, así como la manipulación de cuentas para poder captar inversores. Debido a los actos realizados por involucrados en el caso, en 2013 se produjeron perdidas de casi EUR 800,000,000 y EUR 3,600,000, lo que llevó a la quiebra a Pescanova.

De acuerdo con elcorreogallego.es; Junio 04, 2020: La Sala de lo Civil del Tribunal Supremo rechazó el recurso presentado por Nueva Pescanova a la sentencia dictada en Diciembre 2016, en la que se desestimaba la petición de que la antigua sociedad afrontara el pago de distintas cantidades, acuerdo que tuvo lugar en 2015 entre las dos empresas. El fallo desestimó la reclamación de EUR 1,090,000 retenidos por Pescanova más los intereses devengados desde 2015 así como otros EUR 800,000 para gastos administrativos.

De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Enero 28, 2020: Pescanova SA, la vieja sociedad, iba a ir a juicio en la Audiencia Nacional junto con todos los antiguos altos cargos de la multinacional. Las 19 personas y las 11 jurídicas estaban acusadas de haber alterado los estados financieros entre los años 2009 y 2012 para ocultar las perdidas millonarias de la empresa. Pescanova SA, manifestó que Nueva Pescanova, que surgió tras el concurso de acreedores, se iba a encargar de las consecuencias económicas de la hipotética sentencia condenatoria. Adicionalmente, el juez impuso una multa de EUR 262,000,000 y EUR 348,200,000 de fianza para Pescanova SA.

De acuerdo con europapress.es; Noviembre 28, 2015: La Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) impusó dos puntas a Pescanova por un monto total de EUR 450.000 y otras dos al ex presidente ejecutivo de la empresa Manuel Fernández de Sousa-Faro por EUR 225.000 por infracciones a la Ley del Mercado de Valores, según a la Gaceta Oficial del Estado (BOE), tanto la empresa gallega como su entonces presidente han sido multados por llevar a cabo prácticas de manipulación del Mercado entre Enero 29 y Abril 29, 2009.

row.name: Pescanova, Inc
row.position_or_allegation: Ordered to pay a penalty of USD 35,000 for smuggling - June 13, 2013.
row.details: enforcement: Smuggling | US-United States Attorney - Southern District of Florida | United States
row.profile_notes:
According to United States Attorney - Northern District of New York; June 13, 2013: United States Attorney announced that his office has settled a civil action it brought against Pescanova, Inc. (d/b/a Pescanova USA), an international seafood company with offices in Coral Gables, Florida, based upon the company’s exportation, and subsequent re-importation, of 9,600 pounds of Patagonian toothfish (also known as Chilean Sea Bass or Dissostichus eleginoides) on October 24 and December 15, 2010. As part of the settlement, Senior United States District Court Judge Lawrence E. Kahn issued a Consent Decree which authorized civil penalties, forfeiture and permanent injunctive relief against Pescanova. As part of the settlement, Pescanova will pay civil penalties totaling USD 35,000.00, forfeit USD 96,013.76.

According to United States Attorney - Southern District of Florida; February 03, 2011:  United States Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, announced that the Coral Gables-based seafood company Pescanova Inc., d/b/a Pescanova USA (“Pescanova”), was sentenced in federal District Court in Miami on charges related to the attempted import into the United States of approximately 96,984 Kilograms of frozen toothfish (Dissostichus spp.) from Argentina, with a declared imported value of approximately USD 1,200,000, in violation of the Antarctic Marine Living Resources Convention Act ("Antarctic Act"), 16 U.S.C. § 2431, et sec., and the Lacey Act, Title 16, United States Code, Sections 3372(a)(2)(A) and 3373(d)(1)(A). According to the statement in court and case-related records, in December 2009 Pescanova was the importer of record of four cargo containers of Patagonian toothfish, known commonly in the market-place as Chilean Sea Bass, which were landed at Port Everglades, Florida. The fish were shipped by a company in Argentina related to Pescanova through its parent, Argenova, S.A., an international fisheries conglomerate based in Spain. Pescanova intended to market the product in the United States. United States District Court Judge Ursula Ungaro, who accepted a guilty plea in the case in August 2010, also imposed the sentence. The Court specifically took into account the fact that the illegal seafood product had already been forfeited to the United States and sold for USD1,700,000. Based on representations regarding the implementation of an extensive compliance plan, the Court imposed an additional criminal fine of USD 10,000.

According to United States Attorney - Southern District of Florida; August 24, 2010: Wifredo A. Ferrer, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Florida, announced that PESCANOVA INC., d/b/a PESCANOVA USA, ("Pescanova”), a Coral Gables-based seafood company, pled guilty to charges related to the attempted import into the United States of approximately 96,984 kilograms of frozen toothfish (Dissostichus spp.) from Argentina, in violation of the Antarctic Marine Living Resources Convention Act ("Antarctic Act"), 16 U.S.C. § 2431, et sec. and the Lacey Act, Title 16 , United States Code, Sections 3372(a)(2)(A) and 3373(d)(1)(A). According to the allegations in the Information and statements in court, in December 2009 Pescanova was the importer of record of four cargo containers of Patagonian toothfish, known commonly in the market-place as Chilean Sea Bass, which were landed at Port Everglades, Florida. Pescanova’s intention was to market the product in the United States. The declared wholesale value of the toothfish was approximately USD 1,200,000.
