row.details: enforcement: Organized Crime/Drug Trafficking | PK-Punjab Police (Pakistan) | Pakistan
row.relationships: Zahra, Fatima (Associate; Enforcement); Ali, Muhammad (Associate; Enforcement); Iftikhar, Samina (Associate; Enforcement); Khan, Ayub (Associate; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to the Punjab Police (Pakistan); May 07, 2024: In May 2024, the Organized Crime Unit (OCU) of Lahore police has busted an international gang, including four members of the same family, that was supplying narcotics and party drugs to the upper-class youth. The ‘Jordan Gang,’ including four members of the same family, was operating from Central Asia, Mexico, Canada, USA and some other countries and supplying highly expensive drugs in Lahore and Multan. Efforts of police culminated in a coordinated overnight raid on three locations in Phase VI of the DHA, resulting in the arrest of key members of the gang including Muhammad Ali, Uzair, Muhammad Nadeem, Samina Iftikhar and Fatima Zahra. However, Ayub Jordan is still at large as he is operating from Thailand. After an extensive two-month intelligence gathering and covert operation, the unit busted the gang. He said the elusive gang leader, Ayub Khan alias Jordan, was operating secretly and nobody knew his true identity. The OCU managed to infiltrate Jordan’s network through a plan. Multiple purchases were made to gain the trust of Jordan’s associates, leading to crucial breakthroughs in investigation.

Deals were offered to students and other citizens through fake IDs on social media and the gang was operating many bank accounts in the name of a woman suspect, Samina Iftikhar, and her son Uzair to obtain money. Ayub alias Jordan and Muhammad Ali are her two other sons. Ayub Khan alis Jordan was living in Thailand along with his other family members and Muhammad Ali and Uzair were his brothers. Jordan was operating the network for the last 12 years to smuggle drugs into Pakistan from Canada, the USA and Mexico. Investigation revealed that the gang had purchased three villas in the DHA with money generated through drug trafficking. The family was allegedly using these villas to store and supply drugs in the provincial capital and other cities. During the raid, police seized a huge cache of expensive drugs, a police officer said and added that the seized drugs included 110 kilogram weed, 130 Vapes, 4 kilogram cannabis, 4 kilogram ice, 130 grams cocaine, 5,500 packing materials, 9 CBD vapes, 9 kilogram cannabis chocolates, 18 Vovo Packwoods, 21 element rolling tips, 11 nectar collector sets and 17 Gorilla Glues.

According to the roscommonherald.ie; August 10, 2022: On August 10, 2022, Farah Damji was arrested on by gardaí at a property in rural Co Galway before being brought before the vacation sitting of the High Court in Dublin. The High Court has remanded Damji in custody, who is wanted in the UK to serve out the remainder of her prison sentence for stalking and breaching a restraining order. She has several fraud convictions in a number of jurisdictions, was arrested on foot of a bench warrant issued over her alleged failure to appear before courts that were considering the extradition request.

According to the independent.ie; June 28, 2022: In June 2022, A bench warrant has been issued for the arrest of notorious international conwoman Farah Damji, who lost a Supreme Court bid to prevent her extradition to the UK and has failed to appear before a scheduled sitting of the High Court.

According to the roscommonherald.ie; June 16, 2022: In June 2022, Supreme court upholds decision to extradite on-the-run fraudster Farah Damji to the UK. She will be extradited to the United Kingdom to serve the remainder of her sentence for stalking-type offences and breaching a restraining order after the Supreme Court dismissed her appeal.

According to the irishtimes.com; January 31, 2022: The High Court has ordered the extradition of on-the-run fraudster Farah Damji to the UK, where she is wanted for fleeing a trial. She has been remanded on continuing bail, as the court heard she intends to appeal the decision.

According to the irishtimes.com; August 17, 2020: On August 17, 2020, Farah Damji also known as Farah Dan, was arrested in Dublin. A search was carried out at a block of apartments in Dublin’s north inner city, close to Bachelor’s Walk, where she was located and arrested. She had fled to Ireland while on the run amid a trial in London in which she was convicted and sentenced in her absence. She was convicted in February on two counts of breaching a restraining order, in April 2018 and June 2018. Following her conviction in her absence, she was sentenced in March to 27 months in jail and a European Arrest Warrant was issued for her. She has a long and storied criminal career stretching back to the early 1990s, when she ran an art gallery in New York and East Hampton.

According to the dailymail.co.uk; January 29, 2010: On January 29, 2010, Farah Damji, daughter of multi-millionaire property tycoon Amir Damji, was sentenced to 15 months in prison for a GBP 17,500 housing benefit fraud. She admitted three counts of dishonestly making false representations to Hammersmith and Fulham Council, a letting agency and a landlord. She had already served for three-and-a-half years after being found guilty at Blackfriars Crown Court in October 2005 for stealing a credit card and fraudulently spending GBP 50,000.

row.profile_notes:
According to United States Attorney - Southern District of New York and U.S. Internal Revenue Service; September 12, 2023: Karl Sebastian Greenwood was sentenced to 20 years in prison for his orchestration of the massive OneCoin fraud scheme. Greenwood was ordered to pay approximately USD 300 million in forfeiture.

According to United States Attorney - Southern District of New York and U.S. Internal Revenue Service; December 16, 2022: On December 16, 2022, Karl Sebastian Greenwood, who co-founded OneCoin, pled guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, one count of wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering in connection with his participation in the massive OneCoin fraud scheme.  OneCoin, which began operations in 2014 and was based in Sofia, Bulgaria, marketed and sold a fraudulent cryptocurrency by the same name through a global multi-level-marketing (MLM) network.  As a result of misrepresentations that Greenwood and others made about OneCoin, victims invested over four billion dollars worldwide in the fraudulent cryptocurrency. 

Greenwood and his co-conspirators, including fugitive Ruja Ignatova, conned unsuspecting victims out of billions of dollars, claiming that OneCoin would be the Bitcoin killer.  In fact, OneCoins were entirely worthless. OneCoin operated as a MLM network through which members received commissions for recruiting others to purchase cryptocurrency packages.  Greenwood and other OneCoin leaders also claimed that the OneCoin cryptocurrency was “mined” using mining servers maintained and operated by the company.  In fact, OneCoins were never mined using computer resources. Greenwood was arrested at his residence on the island of Koh Samui, Thailand, in July 2018, and was extradited to the United States to face fraud and money laundering charges in October 2018. Greenwood has been detained since his arrest in July 2018.

row.profile_notes:
According to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; January 10, 2017: On January 10, 2017, The Securities and Exchange Commission announced that the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey has agreed to admit wrongdoing and pay a USD 400,000 penalty to settle charges that it was aware of risks to a series of New Jersey roadway projects but failed to inform investors purchasing the bonds that would fund them.

The SEC’s order finds that the Port Authority offered and sold USD 2,300,000,000 worth of bonds to investors despite internal discussions about whether certain projects outlined in offering documents, including the Pulaski Skyway, ventured outside its mandate and potentially weren’t legal to pursue.  One internal memo noted, “There is no clear path to legislative authority to undertake such projects.” Another memo explicitly identified “the risk of a successful challenge by the bondholders and investors” in connection with the funding of the roadway projects.  But the Port Authority omitted any mention in its offering documents about these risks surrounding its ability to fund the projects.  Its offering documents stated that it issued bonds “only for purposes for which the Port Authority is authorized by law to issue bonds.”

The Port Authority is the first municipal issuer to admit wrongdoing in an SEC enforcement action. The SEC’s order finds that the Port Authority violated Sections 17(a)(2) and 17(a)(3) of the Securities Act of 1933. The SEC’s order acknowledges the Port Authority’s cooperation and prompt remedial acts. The projects at issue have proceeded as planned.

According to money.cnn.com, nbcnewyork.com and philly.com; September 25, 2015: U.S. Department of Justice opens probe into Port Authority of New York and New Jersey. The Port Authority has adopted new ethics rules as federal prosecutors probe potential wrongdoing at the agency, involving billions of dollars in public works projects.

The U.S. attorney's office in New Jersey has been investigating the Port Authority and particularly former chairman David Samson, who stepped down in early 2014. Prosecutors have subpoenaed numerous documents from the agency pertaining to contracts that include two bridge projects and a highway project in New Jersey, as well as the Port Authority's conflict of interest and recusal policies. When Samson was in charge at the Port Authority, United Airlines resumed direct flights to the South Carolina airport near his vacation home. Around the same time, United was pressing for concessions from the agency, including a new hangar at the Newark airport, rent reductions and a commuter rail-line extension that would connect the airport directly to lower Manhattan.

row.profile_notes: According to the timesofindia.indiatimes.com; May 03, 2022: In May 2022, Rajesh Patel was accused of fraud. He and his co-conspirator allegedly cheated two customers of INR 526,000. The complainant and his family were planning a holiday trip to Maldives in March 2022. He visited Balajiholydasindia.com and got the number of Jain who offered a package tour. The complainant then transferred INR 150,000 to Jain in instalments through different bank accounts. The accused then asked for the balance payment but the complainant said he will pay only after the flight ticket gets confirmed. The next day, Patel called up the complainant and said he is sending the flight ticket and demanded INR 100,000 towards the balance payment. The complainant transferred the money but he didn’t get the ticket. He then called up Jain but didn’t get any response. The complainant got suspicious and checked the invoice sent by the accused which turned out to be fake. The complainant said in his complaint that another citizen too was duped in a similar manner by the accused. He has lost INR 276,000.

row.profile_notes:
According to United States - Illinois Investment Policy Board - Prohibited Investment List; Danske Bank, is removed from the Illinois Prohibited Investment List. The company was previously included in the list, deemed prohibited from investment.

According to the Financial Supervisory Authority of Norway; January 22, 2025: On January 15, 2025: the Norwegian Financial Supervisory Authority has imposed a fine against Danske Bank A/S worth NOK 50,000,000 for market manipulation in connection with the issuance of a government bond in February 2023. The Financial Supervisory Authority of Norway believes that the bank allegedly drove up the swap rate, which impacted the bond’s price and yield, and that the trades were carried out based on a deliberate strategy and in a situation where the bank profited from a high effective yield.

Аccording to the French Judicial Public Interest Agreements List; September 18, 2024: On September 18, 2024, the Paris court confirmed the judicial public interest agreement between the Paris Prosecutor's Office and Danske Bank A/S signed on August 27, 2024. A judicial investigation was opened on April 09, 2015 into organized laundering of tax fraud and concealment of organized fraud committed since January 01, 2008. It revealed that the bank's Estonian branch transferred the proceeds of tax fraud committed by an executive of a French company. Danske Bank A/S agreed to pay EUR 6,328,799 to settle the charges. 

According to storage.courtlistener.com: On January 05, 2023, Danske Bank A/S was sentenced to three years of probation for conspiracy to commit bank fraud.

According to the United States Attorney - Southern District of New York and United States Department of Justice; December 13, 2022: On December 13, 2022, Danske Bank A/S pleaded guilty to conspiring to commit bank fraud and agreed to forfeit USD 2,000,000,000 to resolve the United States investigation into Danske Bank’s fraud on U.S. banks. According to court documents, Danske Bank defrauded U.S. banks regarding Danske Bank Estonia’s customers and anti-money laundering controls to facilitate access to the U.S. financial system for Danske Bank Estonia’s high-risk customers, who resided outside of Estonia – including in Russia. The Justice Department will credit nearly USD 850,000,000 in payments that Danske Bank makes to resolve related parallel investigations by other domestic and foreign authorities. Additionally, the SEC announced a separate settlement with Danske Bank. Under the terms of that resolution, Danske Bank agreed to pay approximately USD 413,000,000, which includes a civil monetary penalty of USD 178,600,000, as well as disgorgement that will be credited to any such payments made to the Danish authorities or the department in connection with Danske Bank’s guilty plea.

According to the United States Securities and Exchange Commission; December 13, 2022: On December 13, 2022, the Securities and Exchange Commission announced fraud charges against Danske Bank for misleading investors about its anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program in its Estonian branch and failing to disclose the risks posed by the program’s significant deficiencies. Danske Bank agreed to pay USD 413,000,000 to settle the SEC’s charges.  The Securities and Exchange Commission entered a final judgment permanently enjoining Danske Bank from future violations and ordered Danske Bank to pay USD 178,600,000 in disgorgement, USD 55,800,000 in prejudgment interest, and USD 178,600,000 in a civil penalty.  According to the SEC’s complaint, when Danske Bank acquired its Estonian branch in 2007, it knew or should have known that a substantial portion of the branch’s customers were engaging in transactions that had a high risk of involving money laundering; that its internal risk management procedures were inadequate to prevent such activity; and that its AML and Know-Your-Customer procedures were not being followed and did not comply with applicable laws and rules. The SEC alleges that, from 2009 to 2016, these high-risk customers, none of whom were residents of Estonia, utilized Danske Bank’s services to transact billions of dollars in suspicious transactions through the U.S. and other countries, generating as much as 99 percent of the Estonian branch’s profits. The complaint further alleges that, although Danske Bank knew of these high-risk transactions, it made materially misleading statements and omissions in its publicly available reports stating that it complied with its AML obligations and that it had effectively managed its AML risks.

According to the Central Bank of Ireland; September 15, 2022: On September 13, 2022, the Central Bank of Ireland (the Central Bank) reprimanded and fined Danske Bank A/S, trading in Ireland as Danske Bank, EUR 1,820,000 pursuant to its Administrative Sanctions Procedure for three breaches of the Criminal Justice (Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing) Act 2010, as amended (the CJA). The three CJA breaches stem from the failure by Danske Bank A/S (Danske) to ensure that its automated transaction monitoring system monitored the transactions of certain categories of customers of its Irish branch, for a period of almost nine years, between 2010 and 2019. The root cause of this failure was historic data filters that were applied within Danske’s automated transaction monitoring system, first implemented in 2005 and rolled out to the Irish branch in 2006. Danske failed to consider the appropriateness of these historic data filters within the system or make any adjustments to the system to take account of the specific requirements of the CJA when it came into force in Ireland in 2010. This led to the erroneous exclusion of certain categories of customers from transaction monitoring, including some customers rated by Danske as high and medium risk, which caused the three breaches of the CJA in this case. The Central Bank has determined the appropriate fine to be EUR 2,600,000, which has been reduced by 30% to EUR 1,820,000 in accordance with the early settlement discount scheme provided for in the Central Bank’s Administrative Sanctions Procedure (ASP). 

According to bnn-news.com; December 16, 2020: As of December 2020, Danske Bank A/S is under investigation by US Department of the Treasury, Federal Bureau of Investigations and the US Attorney’s Office in New York over suspicions of money laundering and fraud. Danske Bank A/S has previously reported being under investigation by USA authorities for its suspicious flow of money through their branches in Baltic States.

According to the United States - CBOE Futures Exchange - CFE; January 16, 2020: On January 16, 2020, Danske Bank A/S has been ordered to pay USD 30,000 in penalty for violation of CFE rules. From in or about November 2018 to in or about January 2019, including on six trade dates, Danske submitted simultaneous buy and sell orders in the same VX futures contract expiration at the identical price for the same account. Danske submitted the matching orders in order to rebalance different sub-strategies in the account.

According to challenges.fr and danskebank.com; February 07, 2019: On February 07, 2019, Danske Bank A/S was placed under investigation in Paris, France in connection with an investigation into organized laundering of tax evasion proceeds. Reportedly, between 2007 and 2014, Danske Bank A/S might have assisted in multiple transactions consisting in investing, concealing, or converting the direct or indirect proceeds of the offenses for non-resident customers of Danske Bank’s branch in Estonia. The investigation covers transactions amounting to EUR 21,600,000. Danske Bank A/S was placed under investigation for the first time on October 11, 2017, then the bank was assigned "an assisted witness" status on January 25, 2018. 

According to irishexaminer.com; December 04, 2018: On December 2018, Danske Bank was required by the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority to add the sum of EUR 1,300,000,000 to its capital requirement so as to be prepared to alleviate the consequences of the money laundering scandal.

According to thelocal.dk; November 28, 2018: In November, 2018 Danske Bank was charged with violating money-laundering laws between February, 2007 and January, 2016. The Copenhagen international financial crimes unit SØIK reported that the investigation begun in August offered the ground for the charges.

According to reuters.com; October 04, 2018: Published on that date, Danske Bank A/S is under criminal investigation by United States authorities over a USD 230,000,000,000 money laundering scandal at its Estonian branch. The internal report of the bank said that misconduct stretching from 2007 to 2015 at the Estonian branch payments totaling USD 230,000,000,000, many of which it described as suspicious. Denmark’s Estonian branch were held by entities or individuals in Russia, which is the subject of U.S. sanctions.

According to atimes.com; September 24, 2018: In September 2018, the law firm that conducted an investigation for Danske Bank estimated that the amount of suspicious transactions at the Estonian branch of the company was EUR 200,000,000,000. The money transited through the Estonian subsidiary of Danske Bank between 2007 and 2015.

According to rte.ie; September 21, 2018: As of September 2018, Danske Bank A/S is under investigation by Britain's National Crime Agency. The agency investigates the involvement of the United Kingdom concerning the connection of money laundering at Danske Bank.

According to the yle.fi; August 06, 2018: In the ongoing investigation of Danske Bank a new leak revealed that the sum subjected to money laundering is estimated to be around EUR 7,000,000,000. It is also reported that the money laundered through the Estonian branch of Danske Bank came from Russia, Moldova and Azerbaijan. Danske Bank has started a internal investigation; the results will be revealed in September, 2018.

According to the European Securities and Markets Authority; July 23, 2018: On July 23, 2018, Danske Bank A/S was fined EUR 495,000 by the European Securities and Markets Authority for negligently breaching the Credit Rating Agencies Regulation. Danske Bank A/S issued credit ratings between June, 2011 and August, 2016 without the authorization of the European Securities and Markets Authority. 

According to dr.dk, nyheder.tv2.dk and defensenews.com; July 03, 2018: In July, 2018, in the ongoing money laundering investigation of the Estonian branch of Danske Bank, a new leak revealed the amount of DKK 25,000,000,000 in addition to the previously discovered DKK 28,000,000,000, thus, creating a total amount of DKK 53,000,000. The new amount subjected to money laundering was revealed through 20 accounts which appear in bank statements received from 20 companies that had accounts in the Estonian branch, during different periods between 2007 and 2015. The suspicious amounts were channeled to Danske Bank Estonia from Moldova, Russia and Azerbaijan and into Europe. The Danish investigators are also examining the end-uses of the money laundered for the shipment of military materials through North Korea and Iran from December, 2009.

According to the United States -Colorado Public Employees' Retirement Association: June 16, 2023: On April 04, 2018, Danske Bank A/S was removed from the restricted (i.e. scrutinized) Israel companies list published by the Colorado Public Employees' Retirement Association. On September 22, 2017, Danske Bank A/S is placed on the restricted companies list published by the Colorado Public Employees' Retirement Association.

According to the United States-Illinois State Board of Investment; January 16, 2018: On June 30, 2017, Danske Bank is included in the prohibited list, deemed prohibited from investment for having ties with entities that boycott Israel. 

According to the United States-Illinois Investment Policy Board - Prohibited Investment List; Danske Bank is added to the Illinois Prohibited Investment List, deemed prohibited from investment.

According to danskebank.dk; December 21, 2017: On December 21, 2017, Danske Bank has agreed to pay the fine of DKK 12,500,000 for violating the anti-money laundering legislation. 

According to anklagemyndigheden.dk; December 21, 2017: On December 21, 2017, Danske Bank was fined DKK 12,500,000 for violating the Money Laundering Act by the State Prosecutor for Serious Economic and International Crime. The fine came as a result of a 2016 inspection conducted by the Financial Supervisory Authority of Denmark, which showed that Danske Bank has violated the Money Laundering Act. The bank failed to follow the rules in regard to supervising transactions to and from banks which provide services on Danske Bank's behalf.      

According to euobserver.com; October 13, 2017: The Tribunal de Grande Instance de Paris stated that EUR 15,000,000 of money from organized fraud and tax evasion in Russia were moved through Danske Bank Estonian Branch into France and other EU jurisdictions from 2008 to 2011 via multiple transactions in an organized manner.

According to news.err.ee; September 05, 2017: Between 2012 and 2014, Danske Bank permitted the Azerbaijani regime to send approximately USD 2,900,000,000 of bribe money through accounts in the bank’s Estonian branch to at least two European politicians, a journalist writing regime-friendly articles, companies selling luxury goods, and other influential individuals around the world, overriding money laundering regulations.

According to reuters.com; March 21, 2017: On March 20, 2017, Danske Bank A/S has agreed to cooperate in the investigation conducted by the authorities in Moldova and Latvia. Danske Bank is suspected of money laundering operations handled through their international branches. Between 2011 and 2014, over DKK 7,000,000,000 was transferred to accounts of Danske Bank A/S and another bank. Most of the transactions were made by Danske Bank's Estonian branch.

According to the Federal Bureau of Prisons, information as of December 13, 2017:
Name: TIMOTHY PANGELIN VILLAGOMEZ
Register Number: 00590-005
Age: 55
Race: Asian
Sex: Male
Released On: June 23, 2017

According to the pina.com.fj; June 13, 2013: On June 12, 2013, Timothy Pangelinan Villagomez, former Lieutenant Governor of the Northern Mariana Islands, was resentenced to hundred and eight months imprisonment, or nine years, from the original eighty seven months for his role in the Rydlyme corruption scandal. After an 18-day trial almost four years ago, Villagomez was convicted of conspiracy to defraud the United States, wire fraud, theft concerning a program receiving federal funds, and bribery concerning a program receiving federal funds that involved the Commonwealth Utilities Corp.

According to the saipantribune.com; August 06, 2009: On August 05, 2009, Timothy Pangelinan Villagomez, former Lieutenant Governor, was sentenced to eighty seven months in prison and three years of supervised release for his role in the Rydlyme corruption scandal. Judge ordered Villagomez and the Santos couple to jointly pay USD 346,125 to the court for reimbursement to CUC. Judge also ordered Villagomez and the Santos couple to each pay a USD 400 court assessment fee and perform 200 hours of community service. Villagomez and the Santos couple were found guilty on April 24, 2009, of all charges relating to CUC's purchases of excessive amounts of a chemical, at a 400 percent markup, from companies owned by James and Joaquina Santos.

According to the saipantribune.com; August 12, 2008: On August 11, 2008, Former Lt. Gov. Timothy Villagomez entered a federal court in handcuffs to face an indictment on three felony counts of wire fraud, conspiracy and theft of federal funds, the culmination of an extensive five-month investigation by federal authorities. The indictment, charges Villagomez, Commerce Secretary James Santos, his wife Joaquina Santos-who is Villagomez's sister-and former Commonwealth Utilities Corp. executive director Anthony Guerrero with conspiring to bilk the CNMI government out of thousands of dollars through business deals involving needless chemical purchases for CUC. Villagomez and the Santos' pleaded not guilty to each of the charges against them.

row.addresses: 232 Worth Ave, Palm Beach, Florida, 33480-4615, United States [Business]; United States [Headquarters]
row.position_or_allegation: Compliant filed for engaging in deceptive and unfair business practices - September 15, 2016
row.details: enforcement: Fraud | US-Florida Attorney General | United States
row.relationships: CK Le Salon LLC (AffiliatedCompany; Enforcement); Christopher Kaufmann (AffiliatedCompany; Enforcement); Christopher Kaufmann, Le Salon (AffiliatedCompany; Enforcement); Kaufmann, Christopher (Associate; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to the US-Florida Attorney General; September 15, 2016: Attorney General announced an action taken against a Palm Beach jewelry store and the owner, Christopher Kaufmann, for deceptive jewelry consignment practices. Kaufmann operated under four business names that include Christopher Kaufmann; Christopher Kaufmann, Le Salon; CK Le Salon LLC; and Nikolas, LLC. Kaufmann’s operation is located in Palm Beach County’s prestigious Worth Avenue retail district.

According to the complaint, the stores led the consumers to believe that their high-end jewelry would sell for the amount listed in the consignment agreements. However, once consumers turned jewelry into the businesses, the stores purportedly failed to pay consumers the full amount agreed to in the consignment agreements. After repeated requests to either return jewelry or pay the amount agreed in the consignment agreement, the stores allegedly claimed that the jewelry had been lost, stolen or sold and offered to repay consumers pursuant to an installment payment plan. The complaint alleges that the stores typically paid one payment pursuant to an installment agreement and made no further payments to consumers.

row.name: Nikola Corporation
row.addresses: 4141 E Broadway Road, Phoenix, Arizona, 85040, United States [Business]; United States [Headquarters]
row.position_or_allegation: Ordered to pay USD 125,000,000 in civil penalty for engaging in fraudulent activities - December 21, 2021.
row.details: enforcement: Disciplined/Securities Fraud | US-U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission | United States
row.relationships: Milton, Trevor R. (KeyMember; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; December 21, 2021: The Securities and Exchange Commission announced that Nikola Corporation has agreed to pay USD 125,000,000 to settle charges that it defrauded investors by misleading them about its products, technical advancements, and commercial prospects. 

According to the SEC’s order, before Nikola had produced a single commercial product Trevor Milton, the company’s founder and former Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman embarked on a public relations campaign aimed at inflating and maintaining Nikola’s stock price. The order finds that Milton misled investors about Nikola’s technological advancements, in-house production capabilities, hydrogen production, truck reservations and orders, and financial outlook. The order also finds that Nikola further misled investors by misrepresenting or omitting material facts about the refueling time of its prototype vehicles, the status of its headquarters’ hydrogen station, the anticipated cost and sources of electricity for its planned hydrogen production, and the economic risks and benefits associated with its contemplated partnership with a leading auto manufacturer.

Accordingly it is hereby ordered that Nikola cease and desist from committing or causing any violations and any future violations of Section of the Exchange Act and shall pay a civil money penalty in the amount of USD 125,000,000 to the Securities and Exchange Commission.

According to cnbc.com and dailymail.co.uk; September 15, 2020: Nikola Corporation is under investigation by U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) into short seller claims that the company misled investors. The SEC was looking into whether Nikola may have violated securities laws. Federal investigators are examining whether Nikola, which manufactures electric and hydrogen-powered semi-trucks, misrepresented facts about progress it had made in developing the much-touted technology.

row.relationships: Rivera, Wilfredo (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Ilatoma Gálvez, Manuel (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Nanfuñay Gutiérrez, Juan José (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Martínez Solano, Carlos Alfonso (CoDefendant; AdverseMedia,Enforcement); Zeña Sono, José Carlos (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Los Topos de San Ignacio (AffiliatedOrganization; AdverseMedia,Enforcement); Aldana Picón, Roel (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Cabrera Pastor, Álvaro Leoncio (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Larraín Tello, José Manuel (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Ramos Lamadrid, Juan Javier (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Díaz Fuentes, William Desiderio (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Pisfil Simpalo, Daniel (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Ancajima Sosa, Luis Alberto (CoDefendant; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to Ministerio Público, Fiscalía de la Nación del Perú; February 11, 2026: The Provincial Prosecutor's Office Specializing in Corruption Crimes by Officials in Lambayeque obtained an 18-year prison sentence for the former mayor of the Provincial Municipality of San Ignacio, Carlos Martínez, for the crime of embezzlement. He was also fined 620 days and disqualified from holding public office for 10 years. Along with him, other officials were also convicted of the same crime. Among them were the former manager of Territorial Planning and Urban Infrastructure, Álvaro Cabrera; the former head of Settlements, José Larraín; the former head of Logistics, Wilfredo Rivera; the former head of Treasury, Roel Aldana; and the former assistant to the Works Settlement office, William Díaz, who received sentences of up to 18 years in prison and were disqualified from holding public office. Likewise, José Larraín, Juan Reyes, and Luis Ancajima were convicted as accomplices to the crime of aggravated conspiracy, as they were members of the criminal organization "Los topos de San Ignacio". Manuel Ilatoma Gálvez was also convicted in this case, receiving a sentence of four years and 25 days in prison and a three-year disqualification from public office. José Zeña, Juan Ramos, Juan Nanfuñay, and Daniel Pisfil were also convicted. According to the report, they all embezzled PEN 762,000 in public funds by simulating contracts for alleged services involving the preparation of layout plans and topographic surveys.


De acuerdo con Ministerio Público, Fiscalía de la Nación del Perú; Febrero 11, 2026: La Fiscalía Provincial Especializada en Delitos de Corrupción de Funcionarios de Lambayeque logró una condena de 18 años de prisión para el exalcalde de la Municipalidad Provincial de San Ignacio, Carlos Martínez, por el delito de peculado doloso por apropiación. Asimismo, se le impuso una multa de 620 días multa y una inhabilitación para el ejercicio de la función pública por 10 años. Junto a él, también se obtuvo la sentencia de otros funcionarios por el mismo delito. Entre ellos el exgerente de Acondicionamiento Territorial e Infraestructura Urbana, Álvaro Cabrera; el exjefe de Liquidaciones, José Larraín; el exjefe de Logística, Wilfredo Rivera; el exjefe de Tesorería, Roel Aldana; y el exasistente de la oficina de Liquidación de Obras, William Díaz, quienes recibieron penas de hasta 18 años de prisión y fueron inhabilitados para ejercer la función pública. Asimismo, José Larraín, Juan Reyes y Luis Ancajima fueron sentenciados como cómplices del delito de asociación ilícita en su forma agravada, ya que fueron miembros de la organización criminal "Los topos de San Ignacio". Por este caso, también fue condenado Manuel Ilatoma Gálvez, quien recibió una sentencia de cuatro años y 25 días de prisión y una inhabilitación por tres años. También fueron condenados José Zeña, Juan Ramos, Juan Nanfuñay, Daniel Pisfil. De acuerdo con el informe, todos ellos se apropiaron de PEN 762 000 de fondos públicos, mediante la simulación de contratos por presuntos servicios de elaboración de planos de replanteo y levantamiento topográfico.

row.profile_notes:
According to the US-Texas State Securities Board; September 03, 2009: On September 03, 2009 considered the First Amended Verified Petition and Application For Injunctive Relief, Restitution and Permanent Receivership (the "Amended Petition"), filed by the State of Texas ("State") at the request of the Securities Commissioner of Texas, Denise Voigt Crawford (the "Commissioner"). The Amended Petition asked the Court to (1) issue a Permanent Injunction against Defendants, National Life Settlements, LLC, a Texas Limited Liability Company ("NLS-Texas"); National Life Settlements, LLC, a Colorado Limited Liability Company ("NLS-Colorado"): NATT, LLC, a Texas Limited Liability Company ("NATT"); Howard Glenn Judah, Jr. ("Judah"); and Gregory F. Jablonski aka Gregory F. Jablonski ("Jablonski") (each a "Defendant" and collectively, the "Defendants"), their agents, officers, servants, employees, representatives, attorneys, and any other party in active concert or participation with thern; (2) continue the appointment of Janet Mortenson as Permanent Receiver ("Receiver") for Defendants NLS-Texas, NLS-Colorado and NATT; and (3) enter a final judgment against Defendants.

According to the US-Texas State Securities Board; February 26, 2009: At the request of the Securities Commissioner of Texas, Denise Voigt Crawford (the "Commissioner"), Plaintiff State of Texas ("Plaintiff'') filed an Original Verified Petition and Application for Ex Parte Temporary Restraining Order, Temporary and Permanent Injunctions. Restitution. Disgorgement. and Appointment of Receiver (Petition). The Petition asked the Court to issue a Temporary Restraining Order and, thereafter, Temporary and Permanent Injunctions against Defendants, NATIONAL LIFE SETTLEMENTS, LLC, A TEXAS LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (NLS-Texas); NATIONAL LIFE SETTLEMENTS, LLC, A COLORADO LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (NLS-Colorado); NATT, LLC, A TEXAS LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (NATI); HOWARD GLENN JUDAH, JR. (Judah); and GREGORY F. JABLONSKI (Jablonski) (each a "Defendanf' and collectively, the "Defendants"); their agents, officers, servants, employees, representatives, attorneys and any other party in active concert with or participation with them who receives actual notice of the order by personal service or otherwise; and Sterling Bancshares, Inc. aka Sterling Bank (Sterling); Capital One Bank (USA), N.A. (Capital One); and SLSF Escrow Services, LLC (SLSF) as Relief Defendants only (each a "Relief Defendant" and collectively, the "Relief Defendants").

The Court issued the Temporary Restraining Order and Order Appointing Temporary Receiver of Defendants NLS-Texas and on February 13, 2009 (TRO), which is still in full force and effect.

In support of its determination, the Court makes the following findings:

Defendants are in violation of the Securities Act by selling unregistered securities to the public, selling securities through unregistered securities dealers, salesmen, and agents, and committing fraud and fraudulent practices in connection with the sale of securities, and unless temporarily enjoined, the Defendants will continue to commit violations of the law of the State of Texas, all contrary to the best interests of the general public and of the State of Texas.

Defendants have acted as a dealer, salesman, or issuer, or as an affiliate of a dealer, salesman, or issuer, and Defendants have engaged in acts, transactions, practices, or courses of business declared to be fraudulent practices by Section 32 of the Securities Act and have acted as a dealer, salesman, or issuer or an affiliate of a dealer, salesman, or issuer in connection with such fraudulent practices.

Immediate and irreparable injury, loss, and damage will result to the present investors and future investors who have purchased and will purchase securities from Defendants, and to the general public, unless Defendants are enjoined from promoting, issuing, selling, offering for sale, negotiating for sale, advertising, soliciting, dealing in or distributing any security or securities without complying with the registration provisions of the Securities Act, and from committing fraud and fraudulent practices in the sale and offer for sale of securities.

According to the US-Texas State Securities Board; February 13, 2009: A state-appointed receiver seized millions of dollars in the accounts of National Life Settlements LLC (NLS), a Houston company that the Texas State Securities Board alleges sold fraudulent investments based on life insurance policies. 

State District Court Judge Suzanne Covington of Travis County appointed the receiver at the request of Texas Securities Commissioner Denise Voigt Crawford and the Office of Texas Attorney General. The agencies allege that the investments were fraudulent and sold by unregistered brokers and agents. 

In court documents filed today, the State Securities Board said investors deposited approximately $20 million with NLS from November 2006 through the end of 2008. According to an affidavit filed in the case, information provided to an investigator with the Securities Board indicates that about $2.7 million of that total came from the accounts of retired teachers and retired state employees.

row.relationships: Financial Pacific Leasing (AffiliatedCompany; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; May 10, 2021: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation announced a settlement with Umpqua Bank for engaging in unfair and deceptive practices, in violation of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act (Section 5). Umpqua Bank stipulated to the issuance of an Order to Pay Civil Money Penalty (CMP) in the amount of USD 1,800,000.

The FDIC determined that Umpqua Bank engaged in Section 5 violations related to collection practices involving commercial equipment financing through its wholly owned subsidiary, Financial Pacific Leasing, Inc.. The FDIC determined that FinPac’s collection fee practices were unfair and deceptive. Specifically, FinPac charged various undisclosed collection fees to borrowers whose accounts were past due, such as collection call and letter fees and third-party collection fees.

The FDIC also determined that certain collection practices at FinPac were unfair and deceptive. FinPac engaged in excessive and sequential collection calls to customers, even when customers requested that FinPac stop these calls. FinPac also disclosed information about the customers’ debts to third parties. Lastly, FinPac advised borrowers FinPac would report delinquencies on commercial debt to the consumer reporting agencies, when its policy and practice was not to report such delinquencies to the consumer reporting agencies. Umpqua Bank agreed to the issuance of the Order without admitting or denying these violations. In addition, the Bank voluntarily paid restitution totaling approximately USD 1,628,000 to the 16,902 customers who were charged the undisclosed collection fees.

According to U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; May 06, 2021; Umpqua Bank ordered to pay penalty of USD 1,800,000 for engaged in violations of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act. 

According to U.S. FDIC Temporary Order to Cease and Desist and U.S. Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division; September 27, 2010: The Cease and Desist order against Sterling Savings Bank has been terminated.

According to the U.S. FDIC Order to Cease and Desist and U.S. Washington State Department of Financial Institutions Securities Division; October 9, 2009: Cease and desist order issued against Sterling Savings Bank from the following unsafe and unsound banking practices, as more fully set forth in the joint FDIC and WDFI Report of Visitation dated June 29, 2009. The FDIC and the WDFI considered the matter and determined that they had reason to believe that the Bank had engaged in unsafe or unsound banking practices and violations of law and/or regulations. Sterling Savings Bank  failed to maintain the minimum capital ratio, failed to submit an acceptable capital plan and failed to implement or adhere to a capital plan to which the Regional Director and the Director of Banks have taken no written objection.

row.details: enforcement: Disciplined/Financial Crimes | UK-Financial Conduct Authority | United Kingdom
row.profile_notes: According to the United Kingdom-Financial Conduct Authority; September 27, 2024: The Authority hereby imposes on Starling Bank Limited (“Starling”) a financial penalty of GBP 28,959,426 pursuant to section 206 of the Act. Starling agreed to resolve this matter and qualified for a 30% (stage 1) discount under the Authority’s executive settlement procedures. Were it not for this discount, the Authority would have imposed a financial penalty of GBP 40,959,426 on Starling. Starling grew quickly, from approximately 43,000 customers in 2017 to 3.6 million in 2023. However, measures to tackle financial crime did not keep pace with its growth. When the FCA reviewed financial crime controls at challenger banks in 2021, it identified serious concerns with the anti-money laundering and sanctions framework in place at Starling. The bank agreed to a requirement restricting it from opening new accounts for high-risk customers until this improved. Starling failed to comply and opened over 54,000 accounts for 49,000 high-risk customers between September 2021 and November 2023. In January 2023, Starling became aware that its automated screening system had, since 2017, only been screening customers against a fraction of the full list of those subject to financial sanctions. A subsequent internal review identified systemic issues in its financial sanctions framework. Starling has since reported multiple potential breaches of financial sanctions to the relevant authorities.

row.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Federal Trade Commission; December 11, 2019: On December 06, 2019 Omar Hussain and others were ordered to pay jointly and severally USD 8,877,564 for engaging in deceptive practice. The defendants were permanently banned from the debt collection business and from misleading consumers about debt in a settlement with the Federal Trade Commission. In addition to being banned from debt collection, debt brokering activities, and misleading consumers, the defendants also will be banned from misrepresenting to consumers whether they are attorneys.

According to U.S. Federal Trade Commission; February 08, 2019: On February 04, 2019, a federal court has temporarily halted and frozen the assets of a debt collection scheme that allegedly bilked consumers out of millions of dollars, using deceptive and threatening tactics to collect phantom debts that they did not owe. Omar Hussain and others falsely claimed to be attorneys or affiliated with attorneys to pressure consumers into making payments on debts they did not owe, and threatened to take legal action against consumers if they did not pay. The complaint charged that the Omar Hussain deceptive and unfair tactics violated the FTC Act and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act. Hussain is or was a manager, director, president, or organizer of Trans America, Midwestern Alliance, TACS I,  TACS II , TACS III, and Cedar Rose. He is or was an authorized signatory on the bank and merchant accounts for many of the Defendants. At all times material to this complaint, acting alone or in concert with others, he has formulated, directed, controlled, had the authority to control, or participated in the acts and practices set forth in this Complaint.

row.relationships: Giraldo Atehortua, Sebastián (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Zapata López, Hernan Dario (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Echeverri Giraldo, Juan David (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Saldarriaga Caro, Duban Estiben (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Guisao Serna, Adrián Antonio (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Uribe Zapata, Juan Diego (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Jaramillo Álvarez, Medardo de Jesús (CoDefendant; Enforcement); García Zabaleta, Guillermo José (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Hincapié Henao, Yeferson (CoDefendant; Enforcement); David Uribe, Luis Alberto (CoDefendant; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to Fiscalía General de la Nación de Colombia; March 31, 2026: Published on that date, the authorities were able to charge Duban Estiben Saldarriaga Caro, Medardo de Jesús Jaramillo Álvarez, Juan David Echeverri Giraldo, Luis Alberto David Uribe, Sebastián Giraldo Atehortua, Guillermo José García Zabaleta, Hernan Dario Zapata López, Yeferson Hincapié Henao, Juan Carlos Londoño González, Adrián Antonio Guisao Serna, and Juan Diego Uribe Zapata with conspiracy and aggravated theft. These individuals are alleged members of a criminal network accused of stealing components from communications antenna base stations in the municipalities of the Aburrá Valley. According to the information, these individuals allegedly used tools such as grinders, shears, sledgehammers, hammers, and crowbars to illegally enter the sites and steal lithium and lead-acid batteries, copper cables, and generators. They also allegedly transported the stolen items in vehicles and later sold the batteries and generators at low prices. The defendants did not accept the chartes. Six of the defendants were placed under pre-trial detention in prison and four under house arrest.

De acuerdo con la información, estas personas mediante el uso de herramientas como pulidoras, cizallas, mazos, almádanas, barras, entre otros elementos, al parecer, ingresaban de manera irregular a los lugares para hurtar baterías de litio y plomo, cables de cobre y plantas eléctricas. row.profile_notes:
According to Brazil Administrative Council for Economic Defense; April 24, 2023: On September 16, 2016, the Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE) initiated Administrative Proceeding No. 08012.006043/2008-37 against Marcos Martins Muller and associates, for alleged antitrust violations conduct in the regional distribution and resale of liquefied petroleum gas - LPG. The administrative process was the result of investigations from Operation "Júpiter", launched on April 30, 2010. According to the information, between August 2007 and April 2010, a cartel was formed among the accused to establish similar prices in order to earn profit margins above competitive levels in the LPG resale market in the Federal District. On April 20, 2023, the Administrative Council for Economic Defense determined the judgment of the case in the Agenda of the 212th Ordinary Judgment Session.


De acordo com Brazil Administrative Council for Economic Defense; Abril 24, 2023: Em Setembro 16, 2016, o Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (CADE) instaurou o Processo Administrativo nº 08012.006043/2008-37 contra Marcos Martins Muller e associados, por supostas condutas anticompetitivas no mercado regional de distribuição e revenda de gás liquefeito de petróleo - GLP. O processo administrativo foi resultado das investigações da Operação "Júpiter", deflagrada em Abril 30, 2010. Segundo as informações, entre Agosto de 2007 e Abril de 2010, foi formado um cartel entre os ascuados no sentido de estabelecer preços similares de tal forma a auferir margens de lucro acima dos níveis competitivos no mercado de revenda de GLP no Distrito Federal. Em Abril 20, 2023, o Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica determinou o julgamento do caso na Pauta da 212ª Sessão Ordinária de Julgamento.

Respondents violated § 409.5-501(2), RSMo Supp. 2004, when, in connection with the offer of a security, they made an untrue statement of material fact when they offered to sell warrants to AR while falsely representing on their website and their faxed documents to AR that they were located at“2300 Main Street/Kansas City, Missouri, 64108.” Respondents prohibited from Offering or selling the above-described securities in or from the State of Missouri unless those securities are registered with the Securities Division of the Office of the Secretary of State in accordance with the provisions of § 409.3-304, RSMo Supp. 2004. Engaging in any course of business in connection with the offer or sale of a security in or from Missouri that would operate as a fraud or deceit and that includes the representation, whether in electronic media or otherwise: 1. that the Securities Compliance Department is a securities regulating agency; and 2. that Respondents are located at 2300 Main Street, Kansas City, Missouri, 64108.

row.details: enforcement: Disciplined | UK - Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal | United Kingdom || Disciplined | UK-Solicitors Regulation Authority | United Kingdom
row.profile_notes:
According to the UK-Solicitors Regulation Authority: On November 02, 2016, Roland David Taylor received a written rebuke and was ordered to pay a financial penalty of GBP 1,500. He was also ordered to pay the SRA's costs of GBP 1,350 in investigation. Taylor trades as a recognised sole practice in the name of Roland Taylor & Co Solicitors whose office is at 21 West Drive, Wethersfield, Braintree, Essex, CM7 4BT. Mr Taylor was found to have failed to comply with an order made by the Legal Ombudsman and failed to keep the affairs of a client confidential. He thereby acted in breach of principles 6 and 7 of the SRA Principles 2011 and failed to achieve Outcome 4.1 of the SRA Code of Conduct 2011.

According to the UK-Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal; July 10, 2017: The Adjudicator found two allegations proved, namely that the Appellant Roland David Taylor : Allegation 1: Failed to comply with a decision of the Legal Ombudsman ("LeO") dated July 08, 2015, which directed that Mr Taylor should return the sum of GBP 6,085.93 to Mrs A, by the required dated of August 04, 2015 and was thereby in breach of Principles 6 and 7 of the SRA Principles 2011 ("the Principles"); Allegation 2: Released confidential information about his client (Mrs A) and thereby breached Principles 6 and 7 and failed to achieve Outcome 4.1 of the SRA Code of Conduct 2011 ("the Code"). The Adjudicator decided to: (a) Rebuke Mr Taylor, and to order the publication of this decision; (b) Direct that Mr Taylor pay a financial penalty and to order the publication of this; and (c) Direct that Mr Taylor pay the sum of GBP 1,350 in relation to the SRA's costs of investigating this matter.

row.relationships: Perry, Frank M. (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Vacation Property Services, Inc. (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Wilson, Albert M. (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Vacation Property Sellers, Inc. (CoDefendant; Enforcement); Higher Level Marketing Inc. (CoDefendant; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to U.S. Federal Trade Commission; April 26, 2012: A telemarketing operation that allegedly deceived consumers who were trying to sell their timeshare properties is permanently banned from the timeshare resale and rental business, and from all telemarketing, under settlements with the Federal Trade Commission. The case is part of the FTC's ongoing effort to crack down on con artists who use fraud and deception to take advantage of consumers in financial distress. The settlement order against David S. Taylor contains the same conduct prohibitions and imposes a USD 3.7 million judgment, which was suspended based on his inability to pay.

According to U.S. Federal Trade Commission; March 31, 2011: At the Federal Trade Commission’s request, a federal district court has issued a temporary restraining order against a Florida-based telemarketing scheme that allegedly tricked timeshare owners who sought to sell their timeshare properties. According to the FTC’s complaint, since at least 2006, Vacation Property Services, Inc., two related companies, and their three principals have made tens of thousands of unsolicited telemarketing calls to timeshare owners claiming that they could quickly find buyers for the owners’ timeshares. The defendants allegedly trick consumers into paying large up-front fees, typically using one of two deceptive sales pitches – that they have buyers lined up and waiting to buy the timeshare properties or that they will find a buyer for the timeshare properties within a short period of time. Regardless of the pitch used, the defendants demand that consumers pay an up-front fee, ranging from USD 200 to more than USD 8,000. The FTC’s complaint charges the defendants with violating the FTC Act and the Telemarketing Sales Rule by misrepresenting their refund policies and the existence of potential buyers. The complaint also charges the defendants with calling hundreds of thousands of consumers between November 2009 and November 2010 whose phone numbers are on the FTC’s Do Not Call Registry. In addition to Vacation Property Services, Inc., the complaint names Vacation Property Sellers, Inc., doing business as (d/b/a) Timeshare Experts; Higher Level Marketing, Inc., d/b/a Vacation Property Services; Albert M. Wilson; David S. Taylor; and Frank M. Perry, Jr.

row.name: David W Taylor
row.addresses: Norman, Oklahoma, United States [Residential]; United States [Associated]
row.position_or_allegation: Permanently enjoined from securities related business for violating Securities Exchange Act - July 7, 2006
row.details: enforcement: Wire Fraud/Debarred/Securities Fraud | US-U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission | United States
row.relationships: Deep Rock Oil Company (AffiliatedCompany; Enforcement)
row.profile_notes:
According to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; July 10, 2006: On July 7, 2006, the Securities and Exchange Commission filed a settled civil action in Oklahoma City federal court against David W. Taylor, and his company, Deep Rock Oil Company. As part of the settlement, Taylor and Deep Rock, without admitting or denying the Commission's allegations consented to a final judgment enjoining them from violating the antifraud and registration provisions of the federal securities laws.

The Commission charges that Deep Rock and Taylor conducted a fraudulent unregistered offering of interests in two affiliated joint ventures that were to engage in natural gas exploration and production in the Greasy Creek field in Oklahoma. The SEC's complaint details that, from mid-2002 to mid-2004, Taylor and Deep Rock employed a variety of misrepresentations and omissions to raise approximately $2.5 million from nearly 100 investors. Among other things, the complaint alleges that Deep Rock and Taylor exaggerated or fabricated Taylor's industry experience and prior success in drilling profitable natural gas wells; downplayed or concealed the substantial risks associated with the investment; and grossly overstated the success of the joint ventures' operations. According to the Commission, Taylor also failed to inform investors of his prior conviction for wire fraud and securities violations for offering fraudulent oil and gas investments during the 1950s. 

The SEC's complaint alleges that Deep Rock and Taylor violated Sections 5(a), 5(c), and 17(a) of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 10(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 there under. Deep Rock and Taylor have consented to the entry of a final judgment permanently enjoining them from violating these provisions.

Defendant includes: David W. Taylor

row.details: enforcement: Debarred/Disciplined | US –Financial Industry Regulatory Authority | United States
row.profile_notes: According to United States-Financial Industry Regulatory Authority; June 2016: On April 08, 2016, Michael David Taylor was assessed a deferred fine of USD 5,000 and suspended from association with any FINRA member in any capacity for three months. Without admitting or denying the findings, Taylor consented to the sanctions and to the entry of findings that he circumvented his member firm’s annuity replacement procedures by failing to identify and submit variable annuity purchases totaling approximately USD 700,000 as annuity replacements, even though each purchase was funded by the sale of another annuity. The findings stated that Taylor concealed the replacement transactions from the firm’s supervisory review by transferring the proceeds from the replaced annuity to a firm money market account in the customer’s name. After waiting approximately 30 to 60 days, Taylor then used the funds in the money market account to purchase the new variable annuity. Taylor further concealed that the annuity purchases were replacements by providing inaccurate information on the transaction documents he submitted to the firm and the annuity companies. Taylor earned approximately USD 18,000 in additional commissions by submitting the annuity purchases as new trades rather than as annuity replacements. Taylor subsequently repaid these commissions to the firm. The suspension is in effect from April 18, 2016 to July 17, 2016.

row.profile_notes:
According to elpais.com; October 28, 2021: Luis Bárcenas was sentenced to two years in prison for forgery, fraud and tax evasion. The National Court issued a ruling in relation to the reform of the headquarters of the Popular Party (PP) after having considered proven that Bárcenas paid the Unifica company more than EUR 1,000,000 outside of the official billing and accounting, funds that were not declared to the Public Treasury. According to the Hearing, Bárcenas managed the cash funds that were contributed to the PP as private donations through a parallel accounting, of which the income and expenses were not recorded in the official accounting and, therefore, were not audited by the Court of Accounts. Consequently, a fine of EUR 1,200,000 was imposed on Bárcenas for having been a necessary cooperator of a crime of accounting falsification in relation to another against the Treasury for the fraud to the treasury of the Unifica Corporation Tax of 2007.

According to elconfidencial.com; February 22, 2021: The National High Court agreed to commence the repatriation of EUR 50,342,107 that different convicted persons in the Gürtel case, among whom was Luis Bárcenas, had in Switzerland. The objective was to have at the disposal of the court the amounts that had been blocked in various banks in the aforementioned country, which included Credit Suisse, Lombard Odier, LGT Bank, Banque SYZ and Mirabaud. According to the decree, around EUR 22,400,000 were in accounts owned by Bárcenas.

According to antena3.com; February 08, 2021: On February 08, 2021, Luis Bárcenas was facing trial for corruption, forgery and tax evasion. The case was related to the alleged box B of the Popular Party (PP), which is why Bárcenas was going to have to answer for the irregular payment of the reform of the headquarters of the PP on Genova street and for the purchase of shares of a half with money from box B. Likewise, Bárcenas exposed as responsible for an irregular financing institutionalized since 1982, the old leadership headed by Mariano Rajoy.

According to elmundo.es; October 14, 2020: The Supreme Court notified the sentence of the piece Epoca I of the Gürtel plot (1999 - 2005), confirming the sentences imposed by the National High Court on the main leaders of the corruption network as well as that of the Popular Party. The Chamber upheld the sentence of the leader of the plot; however, it reduced the sentences for several of those involved, among them, Luis Bárcenas, who was reduced to 29 years and one month in prison. The Supreme Court took into consideration the appeal of Bárcenas, resulting in the reduction of the sentence for money laundering, exclusion of the crime of forgery and the acquittal of the crime of procedural fraud.

According to nuevodiariodesalta.com.ar; June 02, 2018: Luis Barcenas was part of the case where the La Moraleja Company was involved in a plot of crimes of corruption and money laundering, in which Ángel Sanchis, Ángel Sanchis Herrero were the main architects after diverting EUR 3,000,000 through the company mentioned. The ruling mentions Bárcenas as a fundamental piece, who granted the aforementioned amount to Sanchis Perales as a loan on behalf of the Sinequanon Foundation, however, the funds came out of the Bárcenas account in the name of the Panamanian foundation that the latter had in the Dresdner Bank of Switzerland towards another of the HSBC in New York in charge of Brixo SA, an entity in Uruguay linked to the Sanchís family. Subsequently, part of the funds were transferred to accounts of another Sanchis company, Argentina's La Moraleja SA, through which the aforementioned individuals devised a complex scheme to reimburse the money to Bárcenas. Consequently, all those involved received their respective convictions after it was verified that these knew the illicit origin of the funds.

According to vanitatis.elconfidencial.com; May 24, 2018: Luis Bárcenas was sentenced to 33 years in prison for money laundering, tax evasion, forgery and fraud. Luis Bárcenas and other associates were involved in the Gürtel case and used Grupo Correa and Partido Popular to issue inflated invoices or invoices that did not respond to real services and were paid out of municipal public funds.

According to lainformacion.com; October 02, 2016: The trial of the case Gürtel was schedule on October 04, 2016. The defendants were 37 people including Jose Luis Barcenas Gutierrez, who were accused of fraud, corruption, financial crimes, bribery, forgery and embezzlement for committing irregular activities developed between the years 1999 and 2005. The oral hearing would take place in the headquarters in San Fernando de Henares.

According to efe.com; April 27, 2015: The Prosecutor's Office requested 5 years in prison and fined EUR 265,000 against José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez for the "Bárcenas case". Based on the prosecutor, during 1990 to 2009, when Bárcenas was Treasurer and Manager of Partido Popular (PP), he received cash funds by entrepreneurs who could not made donations to the party, since it was against the law.
 
According to lavozdegalicia.es; March 06, 2015: The Judge of the National Audience ordered the trial of 40 individuals for alleged involvement in a kickback scheme at the heart of Partido Popular (PP). Jose Luis Barcenas was one of the 40 individuals and master head of the case.

According to 20minutos.es; January 22, 2015: A Judge of the National Audience gave José Luis Bárcenas bail, after paying EUR 200,000. Additionally, Bárcenas must appear before the National Court every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, give his address and remain in Spain. 

According to elmundo.es; February 26, 2014: A report of the National Department of Fraud Investigation (ONIF), revealed that the Former Judge of the National Audience has rejected for the third time a request by Bárcenas Gutiérrez to be release from prison, after disclosure of  two bank accounts in the United States under his name.  Bárcenas Gutiérrez defrauded the Spanish Internal Revenue Office with a total EUR 11,5 00,000 between 2000 and 2011. 

According to lavozdegalicia.es; December 20, 2013: The National Audience confirmed the confinement of Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, since they considered he could escape to a country that would not allowed his extradition.

According to canarias24horas.com; July 30, 2013: A Judge of the National Audience decided to foreclosure of the bank accounts in Spain and property of the former Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP), Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, after the period of time to pay the civil bond of EUR 43,200,000 imposed by the Court expired. 

According to elpais.com; July 23, 2013: The judge in charge of the Gürtel case, Pablo Ruz, requested to the Uruguayan authorities to freeze all the bank accounts under the name of Jose Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez or his company Tesedul, which was allegedly the front for laundering money. 

According to publico.pt; June 27, 2013: The Former Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas, was arrested for flight risk. Bárcenas was accused of allegedly sending large sums of money from the political party's accounts to Switzerland and USA. He was sent to prison without bail, as there was a serious risk of flight, or possible manipulation and alteration of evidence of a false purchase and sale of works of art. Bárcenas was to testify on June 27, 2013, about the entry of EUR 500,000 on his account in the notes of EUR 500 during 2006. Bárcenas claimed the money was from sales of art works. He was being investigated for allegedly committing crimes against the government and against public finance, money laundering, attempted fraud and misrepresentation in commercial document.

According to elpais.com; June 13, 2013: According to the report of the Spanish Tax Office, José Luis Bárcenas and his wife, Rosalía Iglesias, defrauded the Spanish Internal Revenue Service with EUR 1,500,000 in 2002 and 2003. The couple also got tax returns of EUR 21,795 during those years. 

According to 20minutos.es; January 16, 2013: According to the reports that judge Pablo Ruz sent to the authorities, the former senator Jose Luis Bárcenas had EUR 22,000,000 in Swiss bank accounts, that were transferred to another account when he was charged with corruption for his involvement in the Gürtel case. 

According to rtve.es; February 09, 2009: Luis Bárcenas was provisionally indicted for corruption, bribery and tax evasion within Operation Gürtel. The Gürtel case investigated a presumed plot of corruption and influence peddling led by the businessman Francisco Correa, who drew funds from public entities in the autonomous communities of Madrid and Valencia to "obtain their own benefit" and in which several workers of the Popular party would be implicated. Luis Bárcenas was accused of receiving EUR 1,300,000 from companies linked to Correa in exchange for receiving concessions from the party's public events.

Political Party: 
Partido Popular (PP).

Career:
Member of the General Courts, Senate of Spain for Cantabria (March 31, 2004 - April 19, 2010);
Treasurer of Partido Popular (PP) (June 2008 - July 28, 2009).


De acuerdo con elpais.com; Octubre 28, 2021: Luis Bárcenas fue sentenciado a dos años en prisión por falsedad documental, fraude y evasión de impuestos. La Audiencia Nacional dictó sentencia en relación a la reforma de la sede central del Partido Popular (PP) después de haber considerado probado que Bárcenas abono a la empresa Unifica más de un EUR 1,000,000 al margen de la facturación y contabilidad oficial, fondos que no fueron declarados a Hacienda Pública. Según la Audiencia, Bárcenas gestionó los fondos en efectivo que se aportaron al PP como donaciones privadas a través de una contabilidad paralela, de la cual, el ingreso y gasto no se dejó constancia en la contabilidad oficial y, por ende, no fueron fiscalizada por el Tribunal de Cuentas. Consecuentemente, se impuso para Bárcenas una multa de EUR 1,200,000 por haber sido cooperador necesario de un delito de falsedad contable en relación con otro contra Hacienda por el fraude al fisco del Impuesto de Sociedades de 2007 de Unifica.

De acuerdo con elconfidencial.com; Febrero 22, 2021: La Audiencia Nacional acordó poner en marcha la repatriación de EUR 50,342,107 que distintos condenados por el caso Gürtel, entre los que estaba Luis Bárcenas, tenían en Suiza. El objetivo era tener a disposición del tribunal las cantidades que habían permanecido bloqueadas en diversos bancos del mencionado país, en los que figuraban Credit Suisse, Lombard Odier, LGT Bank, Banque SYZ y Mirabaud. Según el decreto, alrededor de EUR 22,400,000 figuraban en cuentas de las que Bárcenas era titular.

De acuerdo con antena3.com; Febrero 08, 2021: En Febrero 08, 2021, Luis Bárcenas estaba enfrentando juicio por corrupción, falsedad documental y evasión fiscal. El caso estaba relacionado a la presunta caja B del Partido Popular (PP), motivo por el cual Bárcenas iba a tener que responder por el pago irregular de la reforma de la sede del PP en la calle Génova y por la compra de acciones de un medio con dinero de la caja B. Así mismo, Bárcenas exponía como responsables de una financiación irregular institucionalizada desde 1982, a la antigua cúpula encabezada por Mariano Rajoy.

De acuerdo con elmundo.es; Octubre 14, 2020: El Tribunal Supremo notificó la sentencia de la pieza Época I de la trama Gürtel (1999 – 2005), confirmando las condenas impuestas por la Audiencia Nacional a los principales líderes de la red de corrupción así como la del Partido Popular. La Sala mantuvo la condena del líder de la trama, sin embargo, redujo las condenas para varios de los implicados, entre ellos, Luis Bárcenas, a quien se redujo a 29 años y un mes en prisión. El Supremo tomó en consideración el recurso de Bárcenas, resultando en la reducción de la condena por blanqueo de capitales, exclusión del delito de falsedad documental y la absolución del delito de estafa procesal.

De acuerdo con nuevodiariodesalta.com.ar; Junio 02, 2018: Luis Bárcenas fue parte del caso donde la Empresa La Moraleja estuvo implicada en una trama de delitos de corrupción y lavado de dinero, en la cual Ángel Sanchis, Ángel Sanchis Herrero fueron los principales artífices tras desviar EUR 3,000,000 a través de la empresa mencionada. La sentencia menciona como pieza fundamental a Bárcenas, quien concedió la cantidad ya mencionada a Sanchis Perales en calidad de préstamo a nombre de la Fundación Sinequanon, sin embargo, los fondos salieron de la cuenta de Bárcenas a nombre de la fundación panameña que este último tenía en el Dresdner Bank de Suiza hacia otra del HSBC en Nueva York a cargo de Brixo SA, entidad en Uruguay vinculada a la familia Sanchís. Posteriormente, parte de los fondos fueron transferidos a cuentas de otra sociedad de los Sanchis, la argentina La Moraleja SA, a través de la cual, los individuos mencionados idearon una compleja trama para reintegrar el dinero a Bárcenas. Consecuentemente, todos los involucrados recibieron sus respectivas condenas después de comprobarse que estos conocían el origen ilícito de los fondos.

De acuerdo con vanitatis.elconfidencial.com; May 24, 2018: Luis Bárcenas fue sentenciado a 33 años en prisión por blanqueo de dinero, fraude fiscal, falsedad documental y estafa procesal. Luis Bárcenas y asociados estaban envueltos en la trama Gürtel y usaban al Grupo Correa y Partido Popular para emitir facturas infladas o que no respondían a servicios reales y se abonaban con cargo a los fondos públicos municipales.

De acuerdo con lainformacion.com; Octubre 02, 2016: El inicio del juicio del caso Gürtel fue programado en  Octubre 4, 2016. Los acusados fueron un total de 37 personas, incluyendo a José Luis Barcenas Gutierrez, todos acusados de fraude, corrupción, delitos financieros, soborno, falsificación y malversación de fondos por cometer actividades irregulares desarrolladas entre los años 1999 y 2005. La audiencia oral se llevaría a cabo en la sede en San Fernando de Henares.

De acuerdo con efe.com; Abril 27, 2015: La Fiscalía pidió cinco años de prisión y una multa de EUR 265,000 para José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez por el "caso Bárcenas". Basado en el fiscal, en el momento Bárcenas fue tesorero y gerente 1990-2009 del Partido Popular (PP), recibió fondos en efectivo por los empresarios que no podían hacer donaciones al partido ya que estaba en contra de la ley.
 
De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Marzo 06, 2015: El Juez de Audiencia Nacional ordenó el juicio de 40 personas por su presunta participación en un plan de sobornos en el seno del Partido Popular (PP). José Luis Bárcenas fue uno de los 40 individuos y jefe principal del caso.

De acuerdo con 20minutos.es; Enero 22, 2015: José Luis Bárcenas fue puesto en libertad bajo fianza por Pablo Ruz, juez de la Audiencia Nacional, después de pagar una fianza de EUR 200,000 impuesta por el Sr. Ruz. Además del dinero, Luis Bárcenas está obligado a presentarse ante la Corte Nacional todos los lunes, miércoles y viernes, dar su dirección y permanecer en España.

De acuerdo con elmundo.es; Febrero 26, 2014: Un informe de la Dirección Nacional de Investigación del Fraude (ONIF), reveló que el ex juez de la Audiencia Nacional ha rechazado por tercera vez una solicitud por Bárcenas Gutiérrez para ser puesto en libertad, después de la divulgación de dos cuentas bancarias en los Estados Unidos bajo su nombre. Tesorero del Partido Popular (PP) Bárcenas Gutiérrez defraudó a la Agencia Tributaria con un total de EUR 11,5 00,000 entre los años 2000 y 2011.

De acuerdo con lavozdegalicia.es; Diciembre 20, 2013: La Audiencia Nacional confirmó el confinamiento de José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, ya que consideraban que pudiera escapar a un país que no permita su extradición.

De acuerdo con canarias24horas.com; Julio 30, 2013: El juez de la Audiencia Nacional, Pablo Ruz, decidió la exclusión de las cuentas bancarias en España y de los bienes de la ex tesorero del Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez, después de que el período de tiempo para pagar el unión civil de los EUR 43,200,000 impuesta por el Tribunal expiró.

De acuerdo con elpais.com; Julio 23, 2013: El juez encargado del caso Gürtel, Pablo Ruz, solicitó a las autoridades uruguayas congelar todas las cuentas bancarias bajo el nombre de José Luis Bárcenas Gutiérrez o su compañía Tesedul, que fue supuestamente el frente para el lavado de dinero.

De acuerdo con publico.pt; Junio 27, 2013: El ex tesorero del Partido Popular (PP), José Luis Bárcenas, fue arrestado por riesgo de fuga. Bárcenas fue acusado por el presunto envío de grandes sumas de dinero de las cuentas del partido político a Suiza y EE.UU. Fue enviado a prisión sin fianza, ya que había un riesgo grave de fuga o la posible manipulación y alteración de pruebas de una falsa compra y venta de obras de arte. Bárcenas fue a declarar el 27 de Junio, 2013, por la entrada de EUR 500,000 en su cuenta en las notas de EUR 500, durante el año 2006. Bárcenas reclamó el dinero de las ventas de obras de arte. Él está siendo investigado por blanqueo de capitales, crímenes contra la hacienda pública, fraude y falsedad en documento mercantil.

De acuerdo con elpais.com; Junio 13, 2013: De acuerdo con el informe de la Agencia Tributaria española, José Luis Bárcenas y su esposa, Rosalía Iglesias, defraudaron al Servicio de Impuestos Internos española con EUR 1,500,000 en 2002 y 2003. La pareja también tiene declaraciones de impuestos de EUR 21,795 euros durante esos años.

De acuerdo con 20minutos.es; Enero 16, 2013: De acuerdo con los informes de que el juez Pablo Ruz envió a las autoridades, el ex senador José Luis Bárcenas tenía EUR 22,000,000 en cuentas de bancos suizos, que fueron transferidos a otra cuenta, cuando fue acusado de corrupción por su participación en el caso Gürtel.

De acuerdo con rtve.es; Febrero 09, 2009: Luis Bárcenas fue imputado provisionalmente por corrupción, cohecho y fraude fiscal dentro de la Operación Gürtel. El caso Gürtel investigaba una presunta trama de corrupción y tráfico de influencias dirigida por el empresario Francisco Correa que se nutría de fondos de entidades públicas de las comunidades autónomas de Madrid y Valencia para "obtener un beneficio propio" y en la que estarían implicados varios cargos del Partido Popular. Luis Bárcenas estaba acusado de recibir EUR 1,300,000 de las empresas vinculadas con Correa a cambio de recibir concesiones de actos públicos del partido.
